scholarships.name: Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship
scholarships.description: Assists Maryland students pursuing cybersecurity related degrees who commit to public service employment in Maryland after graduation. Available to undergraduate and graduate students at participating institutions.

scholarships.name: Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Provides tuition assistance to Maryland veterans, active service members, public safety personnel, and their eligible dependents and surviving family, including children of prisoners of war and those killed in the line of duty.

scholarships.name: Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to eligible Maryland students, including dependents of deceased or disabled public safety and military personnel, attending participating Maryland colleges and universities.

scholarships.name: Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Need based aid administered through participating Maryland institutions for students enrolled in graduate or professional programs such as medicine, law, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, and social work.

scholarships.name: Nikole Hannah-Jones Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to Black students in their senior year at a Howard County public high school who are planning to attend college. Part of the Community Foundation of Howard County scholarship portfolio.

scholarships.name: Carlessia Hussein Minority Scholarship
scholarships.description: Supports African American, Latino, or Native American males enrolled in a Howard County public middle school, funding participation in qualified youth development and college preparation programs.

scholarships.name: John C. Clegg Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to Columbia Clippers swim team participants in grades 9 through 12 who are pursuing post secondary education. Administered through the Community Foundation of Howard County general application.

scholarships.name: Doug Parker Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to Howard County public or private school seniors planning to pursue post secondary education. Applied for through the Community Foundation of Howard County general scholarship application.

scholarships.name: Jon Grove Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to Howard County public school seniors whose lives have been impacted by cancer. Administered through the Community Foundation of Howard County general scholarship application.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Howard County General Scholarships
scholarships.description: One general application opens in late February and gives Howard County students access to more than fifty named scholarship funds. Award amounts and criteria vary by fund.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of the Eastern Shore Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Community Foundation of the Eastern Shore
scholarships.description: More than $600,000 in scholarships awarded annually to students from Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties on Maryland's Lower Eastern Shore through a single online application.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Frederick County General Scholarship
scholarships.description: A single general application opening in March gives Frederick County high school seniors, current college students, and nontraditional students over 21 access to more than 200 scholarship funds totaling over $1 million.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Washington County Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 100 scholarships for graduating high school students in Washington County, Maryland. Most applications open in January and close April 1, with recipients notified by mid June.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Harford County Scholarships
scholarships.description: Manages numerous named scholarship funds for students from Harford County, Maryland. Students apply through the foundation's online scholarship portal each spring.

scholarships.name: Central Scholarship Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need based scholarships for Maryland residents attending any accredited college, awarding an average of $4,000. One application is considered for multiple awards. Serving Maryland students since 1924.

scholarships.name: Central Scholarship Graduate and Professional Scholarship
scholarships.description: Funds Maryland residents pursuing graduate or professional degrees in fields such as education, social work, medicine, and law. Students may reapply annually while enrolled.

scholarships.name: MACPA Educational Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Maryland Association of CPAs Educational Foundation
scholarships.description: Awarded to accounting students who are Maryland residents attending a Maryland college or university and have completed introductory accounting coursework. The foundation awards more than $70,000 across roughly 35 students each year.

scholarships.name: University of Maryland Banneker/Key Scholarship
scholarships.description: The university's most prestigious merit scholarship for newly admitted freshmen. The partial award provides $8,000 per year for in state students, while the full award covers tuition, fees, room, board, and a book allowance for four years.

scholarships.name: Rotary Club of Annapolis Scholarship
scholarships.description: Up to four cash awards for graduating seniors at Annapolis area high schools who plan to attend an accredited college or university and demonstrate a commitment to community service.

scholarships.name: Kiwanis Club of Ellicott City Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Howard County high school seniors who are Key Club members and plan to attend a two or four year college or trade school. Applications are due in mid May.

scholarships.name: CollegeBound Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Administers roughly $3 million in scholarship funding for Baltimore City students each year, including funds of the Baltimore Community Foundation, plus mentoring and college completion support for recipients.

scholarships.name: Baltimore Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: A portfolio of donor established scholarship funds for Baltimore area students, most administered and managed in partnership with the CollegeBound Foundation application portal.

scholarships.name: Prince George's Community College Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: The college foundation offers numerous scholarships for students enrolling at or attending Prince George's Community College, awarded through a single online scholarship application each year.

scholarships.name: Maryland Hispanic All-Star Senior Academic Scholarship
scholarships.description: For high school seniors graduating from a Maryland high school and accepted to an accredited college or university in Maryland. A companion trade and vocational award supports students entering trade or two year programs.

scholarships.name: Asian American Studies Program Scholarship
scholarships.organization: University of Maryland Asian American Studies Program
scholarships.description: Awarded to University of Maryland students engaged in Asian American studies and community work. Funded by the Asian American Studies Program to recognize academic achievement and service.

scholarships.name: Tennessee HOPE Scholarship
scholarships.description: Tennessee Education Lottery merit scholarship for residents attending eligible in-state colleges. Freshmen and sophomores receive up to 2,250 dollars per semester, juniors and seniors up to 2,850 dollars. Requires a 21 ACT or 1060 SAT, or a weighted 3.0 GPA, and one year of Tennessee residency.

scholarships.name: Tennessee Promise
scholarships.description: Last-dollar scholarship and mentoring program covering tuition and mandatory fees not met by other gift aid at Tennessee community colleges and colleges of applied technology. Requires FAFSA, a mentor meeting, and eight community service hours per term. Open to graduating Tennessee high school seniors.

scholarships.name: Tennessee Reconnect Grant
scholarships.description: Last-dollar grant that lets eligible adults attend a community college or college of applied technology tuition-free while pursuing an associate degree or certificate. Requires FAFSA and Tennessee residency; reapply annually through the TSAC portal.

scholarships.name: Tennessee Aspire Award
scholarships.description: Need-based supplement added on top of the HOPE Scholarship for students whose family adjusted gross income is below the state threshold. Adds up to 750 dollars per semester at four-year schools. Requires FAFSA and HOPE eligibility.

scholarships.name: General Assembly Merit Scholarship (GAMS)
scholarships.description: Merit add-on to the HOPE Scholarship for students who meet both the GPA and test-score benchmarks. Adds up to 500 dollars per semester including summer terms. Requires HOPE eligibility and FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Tennessee Student Assistance Award (TSAA)
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for Tennessee residents with significant financial need attending eligible in-state institutions. Awards run up to 2,000 dollars at public schools and up to 4,000 dollars at eligible private colleges. Funded first-come based on FAFSA filing date.

scholarships.name: Wilder-Naifeh Technical Skills Grant
scholarships.description: Lottery-funded grant of up to 2,000 dollars per year for students pursuing a certificate or diploma at a Tennessee College of Applied Technology. Requires Tennessee residency; no GPA or test-score requirement.

scholarships.name: Tennessee Dual Enrollment Grant
scholarships.description: Lottery-funded grant helping Tennessee high school juniors and seniors pay for college courses taken while still in high school. Covers tuition and access fees for early courses and up to 600 dollars per course thereafter.

scholarships.name: Helping Heroes Grant
scholarships.description: Lottery-funded grant for qualifying post-9/11 veterans and National Guard members attending eligible Tennessee institutions. Pays up to 1,000 dollars per semester for full-time enrollment. Awarded first-come to Tennessee residents.

scholarships.name: HOPE Foster Child Tuition Grant
scholarships.description: Grant covering remaining tuition and mandatory fees for Tennessee students who were in state foster care, after other gift aid is applied. Available at eligible Tennessee colleges and colleges of applied technology.

scholarships.name: Ned McWherter Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Prestigious, competitive merit award of 6,000 dollars per year for high-achieving Tennessee high school seniors attending an eligible in-state college. Combines a state grant with an institutional match and requires top test scores and GPA.

scholarships.name: Christa McAuliffe Scholarship
scholarships.description: One-time 500 dollar award for a Tennessee student who aspires to become an exemplary teacher, applied toward an approved teacher-education program at an in-state public or private college. Administered by TSAC.

scholarships.name: East Tennessee Foundation Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Umbrella application covering numerous named scholarship funds for students across 25 East Tennessee counties. One general application matches students to funds by county, school, field of study, and need. Awards and criteria vary by fund.

scholarships.name: Haley Elise Van Pelt Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for students with intellectual or developmental disabilities enrolling in inclusive college or career programs. Applied through the East Tennessee Foundation portal using the VANPELT access code.

scholarships.name: Phyllis Y. Nichols Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Knox County high school seniors planning full-time college enrollment, with preference for graduates of Austin-East, Central, Fulton, or West high schools. Administered by the East Tennessee Foundation.

scholarships.name: Spenser F. Powell Memorial Law Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for incoming first-year students at the University of Tennessee College of Law with an LSAT score of at least 153. Administered by the East Tennessee Foundation.

scholarships.name: Walters State Community College Visual Arts Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for students pursuing a visual arts degree after studying at Walters State Community College. Administered through the East Tennessee Foundation portal.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Middle Tennessee General Scholarship
scholarships.description: Single application matching students to more than 160 scholarship funds serving Middle Tennessee. Funds target specific schools, counties, fields of study, and financial need. The general application opens December 1 and closes February 1.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Greater Memphis Scholarships
scholarships.description: Umbrella program of more than 30 scholarship categories for Shelby County and Greater Memphis students. A single application matches applicants to funds by school, ZIP code, field, and need. High school seniors apply by early April.

scholarships.name: Kylen C. Bares Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Memphis-Shelby County Schools students, with preference for those majoring in math, science, or engineering. At least one award is made annually through the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Dr. William and Helen Lucile Gillaspie Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for history graduate students at the University of Memphis, with preference for those studying Latin American history. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis with a February 1 deadline.

scholarships.name: Harold and Ida Jamison Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for African-American seniors graduating from Booker T. Washington, Hamilton, or Melrose High School in Memphis. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Maxine A. Smith Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Memphis high school seniors who participate in the NAACP ACT-SO academic competition program. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: CFGM Community Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for civically engaged students from metropolitan Memphis who demonstrate academic excellence, community service, and financial need. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Constance Butler Goforth Education Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Greater Memphis students demonstrating academic excellence, community service, and financial need. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Helen Hoffman Education Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for first-generation or disadvantaged Greater Memphis students with volunteer or work experience. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Don Poier Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for well-rounded Shelby County public high school students who show strong character. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Original Fayette County Civic and Welfare League Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for African-American students from Fayette County, Tennessee. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Claude P. Thompson Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Greater Memphis students from non-traditional homes or single parents pursuing higher education. Community involvement is required. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Annie Ervin Willis Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Memphis seniors living in ZIP codes 38106, 38114, 38126, or 38127 who meet a community volunteer requirement. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Charles E. Howard Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for African-American males from the Memphis area pursuing vocational or technical careers. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Edna Fant McConnell Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for single mothers in the Greater Memphis area pursuing career education. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis with an adult-learner deadline in early June.

scholarships.name: Ruth H. Mims Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for education majors attending LeMoyne-Owen College or the University of Memphis. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Joseph W. Westbrook / Eldridge Pete Mitchell Melrose Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for students from Melrose High School in Memphis. At least one award is made annually through the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: City of Memphis I AM A MAN Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for City of Memphis solid waste employees and their families. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Ruby Holmes Hefley Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Greater Memphis students who are children of parents with disabilities. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: FedEx Endowed Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit- and need-based award for full-time undergraduates at Tennessee State University. Requires a minimum 3.0 GPA and demonstrated community service. Funded by the FedEx endowment.

scholarships.name: Dollar General Employee Assistance Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Dollar General employees and their children pursuing adult education, vocational, or four-year college study. Eligibility begins after one year of employment. Dollar General is headquartered in Goodlettsville, Tennessee.

scholarships.name: Kicklighter Family Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for graduates of Raleigh-Egypt High School in Memphis. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Mary A. Jackson Smith / Gloria V. Smith Family Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Memphis-area students attending a historically Black college or university. Administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.

scholarships.name: Virginia Commonwealth Award
scholarships.organization: State Council of Higher Education for Virginia (SCHEV)
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for Virginia residents enrolled at least half time in an approved degree, certificate, or diploma program at a Virginia public two or four year college. Students apply by completing the FAFSA or VASA by their institution's published deadline. Award maximums are set yearly based on state appropriations.

scholarships.name: Virginia Guaranteed Assistance Program (VGAP)
scholarships.organization: State Council of Higher Education for Virginia (SCHEV)
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for dependent Virginia residents who graduated from a Virginia high school with at least a 2.5 GPA and enroll full time in a bachelor's program at a Virginia public college. Renewable with continued academic progress. Awards vary by school and available funding.

scholarships.name: Two-Year College Transfer Grant
scholarships.organization: State Council of Higher Education for Virginia (SCHEV)
scholarships.description: Grant for students who earned an associate degree at a Virginia public two year college with a 3.0 GPA and transfer full time to a Virginia four year college. Base award is $1,000, with an extra $1,000 for engineering, math, technology, nursing, teaching, or science and additional incentive at certain public universities.

scholarships.name: Virginia Tuition Assistance Grant (VTAG)
scholarships.organization: Council of Independent Colleges in Virginia (CICV) / SCHEV
scholarships.description: Non-need-based grant for Virginia residents attending an eligible private nonprofit college in Virginia full time in a non-religious degree program. Undergraduates receive $5,250 for 2026-27; students at Virginia's private HBCUs receive an additional $7,500 annually.

scholarships.name: Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program (VMSDEP)
scholarships.description: Waives tuition and required fees at Virginia public colleges for up to eight semesters for spouses and children (ages 16 to 29) of Virginia veterans who died or were rated 90 percent or more permanently disabled from military service. Virginia must be the service member's home of record for at least five years.

scholarships.name: Virginia G3 Tuition Assistance (Get Skilled, Get a Job, Give Back)
scholarships.description: Last-dollar tuition assistance for lower and middle income Virginia residents enrolled in approved high-demand programs at a Virginia public community college. Households up to 400 percent of the federal poverty level qualify; funds cover the gap after other aid for tuition, fees, and books.

scholarships.name: Jefferson Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship covering four years of tuition, room, and board plus enrichment funds at the University of Virginia. Selection is by school nomination and evaluates leadership, scholarship, and citizenship. About 30 scholars are chosen each year from thousands of nominating schools.

scholarships.name: Presidential Scholarship Initiative (PSI)
scholarships.amountLabel: Full tuition, fees, room and board
scholarships.description: About 200 renewable four-year scholarships each year for incoming Virginia residents who graduate from a Virginia high school, are Pell-eligible with significant financial need, and show strong academic potential. Covers full tuition, fees, and room and board; no separate application beyond the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Hampton Roads Community Foundation Undergraduate Scholarships
scholarships.description: One application covers more than 80 undergraduate scholarship funds for students who graduated from a South Hampton Roads Virginia high school. Most funds assume financial need and full-time enrollment; individual funds add criteria such as school district, major, or GPA.

scholarships.name: AAA Tidewater - J. Theron Timmons Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For high school seniors whose parent or guardian is a AAA Tidewater Virginia member, with a 3.0 or higher GPA, attending a Virginia college or university. Awarded through the Hampton Roads Community Foundation single scholarship application.

scholarships.name: Beach Health Clinic Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Virginia Beach high school graduates pursuing health fields including medicine, physician assistant, nursing, dentistry, dental hygiene, physical therapy, occupational therapy, or speech language pathology. Preference is given to students of color.

scholarships.name: Lori Burwell Ocean Lakes High School STEM Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Ocean Lakes High School (Virginia Beach) graduates majoring in science, technology, engineering, or mathematics. A 3.5 or higher GPA is preferred and AP Calculus is recommended.

scholarships.name: Charles B. Cross, Jr. and Eleanor P. Cross Citizenship Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Chesapeake Public Schools (Virginia) graduates who demonstrate community service and citizenship. Awarded as a one-time, non-renewable merit scholarship through the Hampton Roads Community Foundation.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation for Northern Virginia Scholarships
scholarships.description: One application covers more than thirty scholarship funds for Northern Virginia high school students pursuing a specific field of study or interest. Awards range from $1,200 to $5,000 and some are renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Charlottesville Area Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Umbrella application covering many named scholarships for students in Charlottesville, Albemarle, and surrounding counties. Individual funds set their own criteria by high school, county, major, or background.

scholarships.name: Allen Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Charlottesville High School seniors, with emphasis on first-generation college students. Provides up to $10,000 annually for up to four years to four recipients.

scholarships.name: Charlottesville Promise Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Charlottesville High School seniors, alternative or non-traditional Charlottesville City high school students, and eligible adult students pursuing undergraduate or vocational and technical programs. Up to $13,000.

scholarships.name: Charlottesville 12 Scholarship
scholarships.description: A one-time $5,000 scholarship for Charlottesville High School seniors entering accredited nonprofit colleges. Named to honor the Charlottesville Twelve who desegregated the city's schools.

scholarships.name: Golden Garden Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Buckingham and Louisa County high school seniors, especially first-generation students and students of color, with a minimum 2.75 GPA. Provides $2,500 annually, renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Grace Tinsley Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Charlottesville High School seniors who demonstrate leadership, community service, courage, humor, problem solving, and perseverance. Awarded to four students to support their first two years of college.

scholarships.name: Paul W. Bragg Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Fluvanna County High School graduates. Multiple award levels are offered, including a $40,000 four-year award plus $10,000, $5,000, and $2,000 options.

scholarships.name: South James River Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Buckingham County high school seniors. Ten awards of $1,000 each are available through the Charlottesville Area Community Foundation scholarship application.

scholarships.name: Dean Farms Legacy Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Buckingham County High School seniors, with preference for first-generation college students. Provides $1,000 for up to two years.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation for a Greater Richmond Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Community Foundation for a Greater Richmond
scholarships.description: More than 65 scholarship funds for students living in the greater Richmond region and other Virginia localities, awarding up to $15,000. A single application, opening in February, considers high school seniors, recent graduates, and adult learners.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation Serving Western Virginia Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for graduating seniors, current college students, and non-traditional students in the Roanoke, Salem, Martinsville area and surrounding counties. Each fund has its own eligibility, applied for through one online application.

scholarships.name: VALHEN Adelante Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Latinx/Hispanic Virginia residents who are first-generation college students, graduating from or graduated from a Virginia high school, and enrolled full time at a Virginia college with a minimum 2.5 GPA. Renewable one to four year awards cover tuition, books, and fees.

scholarships.name: Dominion Energy Educational Equity Scholarship
scholarships.description: For students residing in Virginia (and several other Dominion Energy states) continuing to college or vocational school. Awards $5,000 for two-year school students and $10,000 for four-year school students, focused on advancing educational equity.

scholarships.name: VFW Voice of Democracy Scholarship
scholarships.description: Audio-essay competition for grades 9 to 12 students, judged locally through Virginia VFW posts before advancing to state and national levels. Students record a patriotic themed essay for a chance at scholarship awards. Student entry deadline is October 31.

scholarships.name: VFW Auxiliary Young American Creative Patriotic Art Contest
scholarships.description: Art competition for Virginia students in grades 9 to 12 (up to age 18 at local entry) that recognizes young artists and encourages patriotism. Entries are judged through local VFW Auxiliary units, advancing to state and national awards.

scholarships.name: Virginia PTA Scholarship
scholarships.description: $500 scholarships for graduating Virginia high school seniors who are student members of an active Virginia PTA/PTSA in good standing. Categories include four-year college, technical/vocational, fine arts, and special education tracks.

scholarships.name: Virginia Sheriffs' Institute Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Virginia residents in a participating VSI member county or city who are pursuing a certificate, associate, or bachelor's degree in criminal justice at a Virginia college. Full-time students receive $1,000 and part-time students $500.

scholarships.name: Preston Coiner Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Charlottesville City and Albemarle County public and private high school students. Awarded through the Charlottesville Area Community Foundation; award amount varies with available funding.

scholarships.name: Emily Couric Leadership Scholarship
scholarships.description: Recognizes and encourages young women in leadership roles. One senior is nominated from each Charlottesville and Albemarle County area high school; no separate student application is required.

scholarships.name: Trysten Young Memorial Fund Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Buckingham County High School seniors. Two recipients each receive $500 through the Charlottesville Area Community Foundation scholarship application.

scholarships.name: Washington College Grant (WA Grant)
scholarships.amountLabel: Varies by income and school cost
scholarships.description: Statewide need based aid for Washington residents pursuing college or approved training. A family of four earning about 83,500 dollars or less may qualify for a full award, with partial awards up to roughly 139,500 dollars. Apply through the FAFSA or WASFA.

scholarships.name: Washington State Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need based scholarship for Washington students pursuing high demand STEM or health care majors at an eligible Washington college. Funds can cover tuition and other costs such as housing, food, and transportation, plus career support services.

scholarships.name: College Bound Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Tuition plus fees and a small book allowance
scholarships.description: State scholarship for income eligible Washington students who signed the College Bound pledge in seventh or eighth grade. It covers tuition at public institution rates plus a book allowance for students who keep a 2.0 GPA and stay out of legal trouble.

scholarships.name: Passport to Careers (Passport to College)
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to about $5,000 per year plus support
scholarships.description: Scholarship and support services for Washington students who spent time in foster care after age 13 or who experienced unaccompanied homelessness. Funds help with tuition, fees, books, housing, and transportation for up to five years.

scholarships.name: Washington State PTA Scholarship
scholarships.description: Four scholarships for graduating seniors from Washington public high schools that have an active PTA or PTSA and who will start two or four year college in the fall. Selection weighs academics, volunteer service, and a short essay.

scholarships.name: Seattle Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: A single application covers eight scholarship programs administered by the Seattle Foundation, with more than twenty five students funded up to 5,000 dollars toward educational expenses. Financial need is calculated by Scholarship America.

scholarships.name: Innovia Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 400,000 dollars in scholarships each year for students in the 20 county eastern Washington and north Idaho service area who are college bound or pursuing vocational or technical training. One application matches students to many funds.

scholarships.name: Greater Tacoma Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Named scholarship funds for students in the greater Tacoma and Pierce County area, including the Ruth Murphy Evans, Dayton E. Finnigan, and Fuchs-Harden educational funds. Awards support college, university, and vocational study.

scholarships.name: Costco Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: Tuition assistance for high achieving, high need students from underrepresented communities attending the University of Washington or Seattle University. Selection considers financial need and status such as foster youth, first generation, or underrepresented background.

scholarships.name: Latino/a Education Achievement Project (LEAP) Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Washington high school seniors entering higher education who show commitment to advancing the community, strong educational and leadership goals, and financial need from family hardship. Supports Latino students statewide.

scholarships.name: Foster Scholarship for Latino High School Leaders
scholarships.organization: Washington State Commission on Hispanic Affairs
scholarships.description: A one time award that promotes Latino academic achievement and leadership for Washington high school students. Administered in partnership with the Commission on Hispanic Affairs to recognize community leadership.

scholarships.name: AWC Center for Quality Communities Scholarship
scholarships.description: Four scholarships for Washington high school seniors who show leadership in their city government, community, or school and plan to pursue higher education. Recipients also receive a stipend to attend the AWC annual conference. Students are nominated by their city.

scholarships.name: Washington Apple Education Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awards for students with direct family ties to Washington's tree fruit industry, such as work or ownership in apple, cherry, or pear orchards and warehouses. Students planning a career supporting the tree fruit industry may also qualify. Renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Pride Foundation Community Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for LGBTQ and allied students in the Pacific Northwest pursuing college, vocational, or graduate education. A single application considers students for many funds. Applications open in October around National Coming Out Day.

scholarships.name: Leadership 1000 Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need based scholarship from the College Success Foundation for Washington students from low income families who plan to earn a four year degree. Includes advising and support alongside the financial award.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation for Southwest Washington Scholarships
scholarships.description: Both need and merit based scholarships for students in southwest Washington pursuing postsecondary education. The foundation awarded a record 1.44 million dollars across nearly 500 scholarships in a recent year. One application with an eligibility quiz.

scholarships.name: Whatcom Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Named scholarship funds for Whatcom County students, including the Bellingham Scholarship Fund, Bellingham Central Lions Club, and Bellingham Education Association funds. The program has funded over two million dollars in scholarships over two decades.

scholarships.name: WSU Regents Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit award for Washington resident first year students entering WSU Pullman full time with at least a 3.8 unweighted high school GPA. All qualified nominees who complete the admission and scholarship process by the deadline receive the award, renewable for four years.

scholarships.name: American Indian Endowed Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for students with financial need who have close social and cultural ties to an American Indian community in Washington. Usable at public colleges and many independent Washington colleges, prioritizing upper division and graduate students, though all applicants are considered.

scholarships.name: WSSRA Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Washington high school seniors planning a career in education, including teaching, counseling, speech or occupational therapy, social work, or psychology. Includes eight Foundation awards and renewable Robert J. Handy awards.

scholarships.name: Yakima Valley College Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 200 scholarships totaling around 770,000 dollars for students attending Yakima Valley College. One application matches students to funds based on field of study, need, and academics. FAFSA or WASFA is not required and most funds require only a 2.0 GPA.

scholarships.name: Washington State Governors' Scholarship for Foster Youth
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Washington young people from foster care who have a high school diploma or equivalent and plan to enroll in college. Awards range from 2,000 to 4,000 dollars per year and can be used for up to five years toward an undergraduate degree.

scholarships.name: TCC Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: About 200 scholarships totaling over 350,000 dollars each year for students planning to attend Tacoma Community College. Applications for the coming academic year open January 1 and close March 31, with awards made from May through August.

scholarships.name: Hispanic Metropolitan Chamber Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Scholarships for students attending or having attended high school in Clark County, Washington or the Portland metro area who maintain at least a 3.0 GPA. Supports Latino students continuing to higher education.

scholarships.name: WE Communications Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for permanent residents of Washington or Oregon who are current HBCU college juniors or seniors pursuing a career in communications. Supports underrepresented students entering the communications field.

scholarships.name: GSBA Scholarship & Education Fund
scholarships.organization: GSBA (Washington State's LGBTQ Chamber of Commerce)
scholarships.description: Scholarships for LGBTQ and actively allied students who are Washington State residents with a vision for inclusion and equity. Students may attend any accredited college, university, or trade school in the United States. Applications open on National Coming Out Day.

scholarships.name: Washington State Elks Association Vocational Grant
scholarships.description: Grant for Washington graduating high school seniors or GED students pursuing a vocational or technical course at a community college or technical school. Funds cover tuition, fees, books, and supplies, with selection based on motivation, need, and skills.

scholarships.name: Washington State Nurses Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for pre-licensure RN, RN to BSN, and graduate nursing students attending school in Washington or who are Washington residents attending nursing school. Awards recognize academic performance, leadership, and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Inland Empire Nurses Association Scholarship
scholarships.description: Up to ten scholarships for nursing students within the Inland Empire counties of Adams, Lincoln, Pend Oreille, Spokane, Stevens, and Whitman, or residents of the region attending any nursing school. Awarded with a Washington State Nurses Foundation scholarship.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of North Central Washington Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Community Foundation of North Central Washington
scholarships.description: Over 130 scholarships for north central Washington students attending any college or university, including the Wenatchee High School Alumni Foundation, Wenatchee Exchange Club, and Junior Service League of Wenatchee funds. Applications open January 1.

scholarships.name: Kitsap Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships from many donor and civic funds for Kitsap County students. Most applications are accepted January 1 through February 28, with a review committee of community members selecting recipients that fit each fund's goals.

scholarships.name: Whatcom Community College Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for students attending Whatcom Community College in Bellingham, with over 565,000 dollars awarded to more than 300 scholars in a recent year. A single application considers current and incoming students for many funds.

scholarships.name: Seattle Colleges Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: One application qualifies current and incoming Seattle Colleges students for scholarships up to 5,000 dollars for the coming academic year. Awards support students across North, Central, and South Seattle College campuses.

scholarships.name: WA Grant for Apprenticeship
scholarships.description: Washington College Grant funding for students enrolled in registered apprenticeship programs. The maximum award equals 50 percent of the maximum award for students at public two year institutions, helping cover apprenticeship costs.

scholarships.name: Latino Educational Training Institute Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Washington State Commission on Hispanic Affairs (HSF partnership)
scholarships.description: Scholarships promoted through the Washington State Commission on Hispanic Affairs in partnership with the Hispanic Scholarship Fund, ranging from 500 to 5,000 dollars for Latino students. Applications open January 1 and close in April.

scholarships.name: Alabama Student Assistance Program (ASAP)
scholarships.description: Need based grant for Alabama residents enrolled at participating Alabama colleges. Jointly funded by the state and federal government and awarded through the school financial aid office based on FAFSA. Priority to students with the greatest financial need.

scholarships.name: Alabama G.I. Dependents' Scholarship Program
scholarships.amountLabel: Tuition, fees and books (up to 10 semesters)
scholarships.description: Covers tuition, mandatory fees, textbooks and supplies at Alabama public colleges for the dependent children, spouses and widows of qualifying Alabama veterans who are permanently disabled or rated at a service connected level. Dependent children must apply before age 26.

scholarships.name: Alabama National Guard Educational Assistance Program (ANGEAP)
scholarships.description: Tuition assistance for active members in good standing of the Alabama National Guard who are enrolled at eligible Alabama public colleges. Award amount is need based with a minimum benefit and is applied toward tuition and fees.

scholarships.name: Police Officers' and Firefighters' Survivors Educational Assistance Program (POFSEAP)
scholarships.amountLabel: Full tuition, fees, books and supplies
scholarships.description: Waives tuition, fees, books and supplies at Alabama public colleges for the dependents and spouses of Alabama police officers and firefighters killed in the line of duty. No award cap.

scholarships.name: Alabama Scholarship for Dependents of Blind Parents
scholarships.description: Waives tuition and fees at Alabama public colleges for students from households where the head of family is legally blind and meets income limits. Students must begin within two years of high school and before age 23.

scholarships.name: Alabama Math and Science Teacher Education Program (AMSTEP)
scholarships.description: Federal student loan repayment for graduates who become full time secondary math or science teachers in Alabama public schools. Base benefit is $3,750 per semester worked with an additional supplement for teaching in acute shortage areas.

scholarships.name: UA Recognition Scholarship
scholarships.description: Automatic in-state freshman merit award for Alabama residents admitted to The University of Alabama. Awarded to students with a 3.0 to 3.49 GPA and a 25 ACT (or 1200 SAT) or a 3.5+ GPA with a 24 ACT. No separate scholarship application required.

scholarships.name: UA Crimson Achievement Scholarship
scholarships.description: Automatic in-state freshman merit award for Alabama residents at The University of Alabama with a 3.0 to 3.49 GPA and a 26 ACT (1230 SAT) or a 3.5+ GPA with a 25 ACT. Awarded automatically to admitted students who meet the criteria by the deadline.

scholarships.name: UA Legends Scholarship
scholarships.description: Automatic in-state freshman merit award for Alabama residents at The University of Alabama with a 3.0 to 3.49 GPA and a 27 ACT (1260 SAT) or a 3.5+ GPA with a 26 ACT. No separate application needed beyond admission.

scholarships.name: UA Capstone Scholarship
scholarships.description: Automatic in-state freshman merit award for Alabama residents at The University of Alabama with a 3.0 to 3.49 GPA and a 28 ACT (1300 SAT) or a 3.5+ GPA with a 27 ACT.

scholarships.name: UA Foundation in Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.description: Top automatic in-state freshman merit award for Alabama residents at The University of Alabama with a 30 to 36 ACT (1360+ SAT) and a 3.0 to 3.49 GPA, or a 29 ACT with a 3.5+ GPA. Higher qualifiers may receive the Presidential (tuition) award.

scholarships.name: UAB Presidential Scholarship (In-State)
scholarships.description: Automatic merit scholarship for in-state freshmen at UAB with a 3.5+ GPA and a 30 to 36 ACT (1360 to 1600 SAT). Renewable for four years. Test-optional applicants may qualify for comparable awards with a 3.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: UAB Provost Scholarship (In-State)
scholarships.description: Automatic merit scholarship for in-state freshmen at UAB with a 3.5+ GPA and 27 to 29 ACT (1260 to 1350 SAT), or a 3.0 to 3.49 GPA with a 30 to 36 ACT. Renewable for four years.

scholarships.name: UAB Green & Gold Scholarship (In-State)
scholarships.description: Automatic merit scholarship for in-state freshmen at UAB with a 3.5+ GPA and a 24 to 26 ACT (1160 to 1250 SAT), or a 3.0 to 3.49 GPA with a 27 to 29 ACT. Renewable for four years.

scholarships.name: Auburn University Competitive Merit Scholarship (In-State)
scholarships.description: Competitive merit scholarships for Alabama resident freshmen admitted through Early Action. Students with a complete admission file by December 1 who are admitted by early February are automatically considered based on high school GPA and test scores, with no separate application.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Greater Birmingham Scholarship
scholarships.description: Flagship scholarship for graduating seniors in the Birmingham City public school system. The top scholar receives $40,000, the second $32,000 and the third $20,000, disbursed over four years of undergraduate study.

scholarships.name: Maria Campbell / Bouchelle Scholarship for Children of Episcopal Clergy
scholarships.description: Scholarship for children of Episcopal Church clergy who are canonically resident in the Episcopal Diocese of Alabama. Awards support undergraduate and graduate study, with preference to applicants attending the University of the South (Sewanee).

scholarships.name: Central Alabama Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Umbrella of donor established scholarship funds administered by the Central Alabama Community Foundation in the Montgomery region. Individual funds have different criteria; most applications share an April 1 deadline through the foundation portal.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of South Alabama Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 40 donor established scholarship funds for students in the Mobile and south Alabama region, supporting certificate programs, two and four year degrees and graduate study. Applicants apply through the foundation online portal; each fund sets its own criteria and deadline.

scholarships.name: Vector Community Scholars Defense Industry Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Huntsville and Madison County students whose parent or guardian works or worked in the space, security or defense industry. Requires a minimum 3.0 GPA and plans for full time enrollment at an accredited two or four year college.

scholarships.name: Alabama A&M University STEM Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: Assists incoming college freshmen with demonstrated financial need who plan to pursue a STEM degree through the College of Engineering, Technology and Physical Sciences at Alabama A&M University, a historically Black university in Huntsville.

scholarships.name: Linly Heflin Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for female Alabama residents attending an accredited four year Alabama college or university. Requires a minimum 3.2 high school GPA, a minimum 23 ACT and demonstrated financial need. Pays $5,000 per semester for up to eight semesters.

scholarships.name: CollegeCounts Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Office of the Alabama State Treasurer
scholarships.description: Need based award for Alabama high school seniors and first time freshmen enrolling at an eligible Alabama institution. Requires a minimum 2.75 GPA and an ACT of 26 or below. Funded by the CollegeCounts 529 Fund with no taxpayer dollars.

scholarships.name: Smith Scholarship Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Largest private scholarship program exclusively for graduating Alabama high school and home school seniors planning to enroll at an Alabama college, university, community college or technical school. Awards are based on financial need, academics, community service and program participation, with mentoring support.

scholarships.name: Regions Riding Forward Scholarship Contest
scholarships.description: Quarterly essay and video contest open to high school seniors and college students who reside in a Regions Bank state including Alabama. Applicants submit a 500 word essay or three minute video about a person who inspired them. Requires a minimum 2.0 GPA. Four $8,000 awards per quarter.

scholarships.name: J.L. Bedsole Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarship for high school seniors in Mobile, Baldwin, Washington, Clarke and Monroe counties in southwest Alabama. Requires a minimum 2.5 unweighted GPA through junior year and a minimum 21 ACT. Two phase application with a November Phase I deadline.

scholarships.name: APF Community Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for high school seniors residing in an Alabama county within the Alabama Power service territory. Requires a minimum 3.0 GPA and full time undergraduate enrollment. Counties in far north Alabama (including Madison, Morgan, Limestone) are not eligible. Administered by Scholarship America.

scholarships.name: Alabama Farmers Agriculture Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Alabama Farmers Federation members or children of members under age 25. Up to 67 awards of $2,000 go to agriculture or forestry majors at Auburn, Alabama A&M or Tuskegee, plus 100 awards of $1,000 for students at any Alabama school.

scholarships.name: Alabama Cattlemen's Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Alabama high school seniors and college students pursuing careers connected to the beef and cattle industry. Administered by the Alabama Cattlemen's Foundation, the charitable arm of the Alabama Cattlemen's Association.

scholarships.name: AGC of Alabama Education Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Alabama students pursuing construction management, civil engineering, building science and skilled construction trades. Supports the pipeline of future commercial construction professionals in the state.

scholarships.name: Alabama Home Builders Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Alabama students pursuing construction trades and construction science careers such as carpentry, plumbing, electrical, HVAC and residential building. Supports workforce development for the state home building industry.

scholarships.name: Cabaniss, Johnston Law School Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Alabama resident law students entering their second year at an Alabama law school. Administered by the Alabama Law Foundation to support future Alabama attorneys.

scholarships.name: Kids' Chance of Alabama Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Alabama Law Foundation / Kids' Chance of Alabama
scholarships.description: Scholarship for children whose parent was killed or permanently and totally disabled in a work related accident covered by Alabama workers' compensation. Helps affected families afford post secondary education.

scholarships.name: Alabama Space Grant Consortium Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: NASA affiliated scholarships for undergraduates in STEM fields and pre-service STEM teachers at member Alabama institutions. Supports students pursuing aerospace and space related science and engineering careers. U.S. citizenship required.

scholarships.name: Alabama Grocers Education Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for employees and dependents of Alabama grocery companies that are members of the Alabama Grocers Association. Supports continuing education for the state's grocery and food retail workforce and their families.

scholarships.name: Boettcher Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship covering tuition, fees and living support for four years at any accredited Colorado college or university. Open to graduating Colorado high school seniors who lived in Colorado through their junior and senior years, or registered members of a federally recognized American Indian Tribe with historical ties to Colorado.

scholarships.name: Daniels Scholarship Program
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to full cost of attendance
scholarships.description: Four-year college scholarship for graduating high school seniors from Colorado who plan to attend the college of their choice. Requires a minimum 3.0 GPA and household income at or below program limits. Covers costs not met by other aid.

scholarships.name: DSF Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable need-based scholarship for Denver Public Schools graduates enrolling full-time at a DSF-approved Colorado college partner. Requires a qualifying Student Aid Index and application within one year of high school graduation.

scholarships.name: Colorado Opportunity Scholarship Initiative (COSI) Matching Student Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need-based scholarship for Colorado residents, including ASSET students, attending a Colorado public institution of higher education. Awards are matched by partner institutions. Requires completion of the CASFA or FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Latin American Educational Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Colorado residents of Latino heritage or those who demonstrate a commitment to the Latino community. Open to undergraduate students including trade, certificate, two-year and four-year learners, regardless of documentation or citizenship status.

scholarships.name: El Pomar Scholars Program
scholarships.organization: El Pomar Foundation (at Colorado State University)
scholarships.description: Leadership scholarship for Colorado State University students in good standing who demonstrate leadership, teamwork and community involvement. Applicants are sophomores, juniors or seniors.

scholarships.name: El Pomar Student Leadership Experience (SLE) Scholarship
scholarships.organization: El Pomar Foundation (CU Boulder President's Leadership Class)
scholarships.description: Leadership program providing tuition assistance for students at Colorado campuses in the Colorado Leadership Alliance. Scholars complete a year-long nonprofit service project and leadership retreats.

scholarships.name: Pikes Peak State College Foundation General Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit and need-based scholarships for students attending Pikes Peak State College in Colorado Springs. Most awards are need-based and require a current FAFSA or CASFA on file. Spring application awards Spring 2027 funds.

scholarships.name: Colorado Masons' Benevolent Fund Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable four-year scholarship awarded for leadership, maturity, need and scholastic ability. Applicants must be graduating seniors from a Colorado public high school who will attend a Colorado institution of higher learning. Requires a FAFSA and four letters of recommendation.

scholarships.name: Western Colorado Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: A single common application covering dozens of donor-established scholarships for students on the Western Slope of Colorado. Most are for graduating high school seniors; some serve returning adult learners and vocational students.

scholarships.name: Genevieve Clough Scholarship
scholarships.description: Donor-established scholarship administered by the Western Colorado Community Foundation for Western Slope students pursuing higher education. Awarded through the foundation's scholarship program.

scholarships.name: The Denver Foundation Community Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship supporting first-generation, economically disadvantaged students enrolled or planning to enroll at a Colorado accredited public post-secondary institution. Requires demonstrated economic hardship through the FAFSA or CASFA, community involvement and a minimum 2.25 GPA.

scholarships.name: Excelsior Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: Need-based scholarship for Colorado residents enrolling at an accredited vocational or technical school, community college or university. Requires a minimum 2.5 GPA. Emancipated and foster care youth are especially encouraged to apply.

scholarships.name: Reisher Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Merit and need scholarship for Colorado residents who are rising college sophomores and community college transfer students attending partnered Colorado public universities. Requires a cumulative 3.0 GPA. Awards cover unmet financial need.

scholarships.name: Reisher Graduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship extending Reisher Scholars support to eligible graduate students in Colorado who continue their education. Awarded to help students finish degrees with minimal educational debt.

scholarships.name: Boulder Rotary Club Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for graduating seniors from the Boulder Valley School District based on academic achievement, volunteer service, extracurricular involvement and potential for college success.

scholarships.name: Cedaredge Rotary Club Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Multiple renewable scholarships for graduating seniors from the Surface Creek Valley pursuing higher education or vocational training. Awards two $2,500 scholarships renewable up to four years and three $2,000 scholarships renewable up to two years.

scholarships.name: Sachs Foundation Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: Flagship scholarship for Colorado high school seniors who identify as Black and have been full-time Colorado residents for at least three years. Awarded on academic achievement, financial need and character.

scholarships.name: Colorado Nurses Association Nightingale Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Colorado resident nursing students who are Colorado Nurses Association or Colorado Student Nurses Association members. Open to second-year ASN, third/fourth-year BSN, and graduate nursing students. Undergraduates need a 3.25 GPA, graduates a 3.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: Colorado Garden Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Horticulture-related scholarships for Colorado resident college students, including a four-year full-ride award for an incoming freshman. Applicants must major in a plant or agriculture field and maintain a 2.5 GPA plus community service hours.

scholarships.name: Colorado DECA Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit-based scholarship for active Colorado DECA senior high school members planning full-time two- or four-year study in marketing, entrepreneurship, finance, hospitality or management. Includes CBAM awards for active DECA participants.

scholarships.name: Colorado Farm Show Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships supporting Colorado students pursuing agriculture and related fields of study. Applications are accepted through the Colorado Farm Show, which serves the Greeley and northern Colorado agricultural community.

scholarships.name: J. Robert Young Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for graduating high school students in Alpine Bank service areas across Colorado who plan to study business or a business-related field at a Colorado college or university. Requires a minimum 2.75 GPA.

scholarships.name: Alpine Bank First-Generation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarship for a first-generation graduating senior from each of 15 high schools within the Colorado Mountain College district. Provides two years of support toward tuition, books and fees.

scholarships.name: Greenhouse Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Boulder-based whole-person college program for high-performing students from low-income communities. Requires a 3.5 GPA and household income no greater than $80,000, plus leadership and community commitment. Provides tuition awards, mentorship and professional networking.

scholarships.name: Montrose Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Multiple donor-established scholarships for graduating high school seniors and students in the Montrose, Delta and Ouray county area of Colorado pursuing higher education or vocational training.

scholarships.name: I Have A Dream Foundation of Boulder County Scholarship
scholarships.organization: I Have A Dream Foundation of Boulder County
scholarships.description: Scholarship support for Dreamer students in Boulder County, Colorado who complete the program's long-term mentoring and college-access pathway. Serves students from low-income communities pursuing post-secondary education.

scholarships.name: Colorado Women's Bar Association Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for second- and third-year law students at the University of Colorado School of Law and the University of Denver Sturm College of Law who are CWBA members, demonstrate financial need and show interest in advancing women in the law.

scholarships.name: Jack Agee Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Pikes Peak Community Foundation (Pikes Peak Kiwanis)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Pikes Peak area high school seniors with a minimum 3.0 GPA who will attend an accredited Colorado college or university full-time. Requires a character reference and a personal recommendation.

scholarships.name: North Colorado Springs Rotary Club Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: North Colorado Springs Rotary Club Foundation
scholarships.description: Scholarship awarded to graduating seniors from the AVID Program at Doherty High School in Colorado Springs. The Rotary scholarship committee reviews applications and conducts interviews.

scholarships.name: Emily Griffith Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships and wraparound financial support for students at Emily Griffith Technical College in Denver, helping students complete workforce training without debt. More than 500 students receive scholarships each year.

scholarships.name: Colorado Farm Bureau Scholarship
scholarships.description: Collegiate and At-Large scholarships for Colorado Farm Bureau members pursuing higher education. Rewards leadership, community service and commitment to agriculture. Applicants must maintain a minimum 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: North Star Promise Scholarship
scholarships.description: Last-dollar program covering remaining tuition and fees at eligible Minnesota colleges for state residents with family adjusted gross income below 80,000 dollars. Requires the FAFSA or Minnesota Dream Act application.

scholarships.name: Minnesota State Grant
scholarships.description: The state's largest need-based grant program, awarding over 224 million dollars annually to Minnesota residents attending eligible in-state colleges, universities, and career schools. Award is based on family income and cost of attendance.

scholarships.name: Minnesota Future Together Grants
scholarships.description: Tuition-free pathway support for Minnesota residents pursuing high-demand career training and workforce programs at eligible institutions. Administered as part of the state's tuition-free program suite.

scholarships.name: American Indian Scholars Program
scholarships.description: First-dollar tuition- and fee-free pathway at Minnesota State and University of Minnesota campuses for enrolled citizens of federally recognized American Indian tribes or Canadian First Nations who are Minnesota residents.

scholarships.name: Minnesota Indian Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Need-based postsecondary financial assistance for students who are one-fourth or more American Indian ancestry or an enrolled member of a federally recognized tribe or Canadian First Nation, attending eligible Minnesota schools.

scholarships.name: Get Ready Student Success Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Minnesota Office of Higher Education (Get Ready)
scholarships.description: For students graduating from a Get Ready partner high school who attend an accredited Minnesota institution. Awards 1,000 per year at two-year schools and 3,000 per year at four-year schools.

scholarships.name: Page Grant
scholarships.description: Grants for Minnesota students of color attending Minnesota postsecondary schools. Page Scholars complete 50 service hours per year mentoring and tutoring younger children in their communities.

scholarships.name: Wallin Education Partners 4-Year Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need-based scholarship plus advising for graduating seniors from approved Minnesota high schools who attend a nonprofit four-year school in MN, IA, ND, SD, WI, or any HBCU. Minimum 3.0 GPA and demonstrated financial need.

scholarships.name: Wallin Opportunity Pathway Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need-based scholarship and advising for graduating seniors from approved Minnesota high schools planning to attend specific partner community and technical colleges in Minnesota.

scholarships.name: Kao Kalia Yang Scholarship
scholarships.description: Five renewable scholarships for Hmong American high school seniors entering a four-year or community college full time. Minimum 2.8 GPA; students demonstrating financial need are encouraged to apply.

scholarships.name: Xiong United of MN Scholarship
scholarships.description: Ten scholarships for Hmong Minnesota residents of the Xiong clan who are high school seniors or current college students. Recipients commit to at least 8 volunteer hours with the organization.

scholarships.name: Latino Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: At least 11 awards for students of Latin American background attending U.S. postsecondary programs. 5,000 for four-year colleges and 2,500 for two-year or associate programs. Administered from Minnesota by LEDC.

scholarships.name: Minnesota Masonic Charities Signature Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship for Minnesota high school or home school seniors with a minimum 3.0 GPA attending a Minnesota college or university. Renewable for up to three additional years. No Masonic affiliation required.

scholarships.name: Minnesota Masonic Charities Legacy Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship for current college undergraduates with a minimum 3.0 GPA attending a Minnesota community, technical, or trade school. Renewable up to three years. No Masonic affiliation required.

scholarships.name: Minnesota Masonic Charities Heritage Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for trade, technical, and two-year college students attending Minnesota institutions. Renewable for up to one additional year in some programs. No Masonic affiliation required.

scholarships.name: Minnesota Masonic Charities Selfless Scholar Scholarship
scholarships.description: One-time award recognizing high school and college students nominated for selfless service, attending any accredited U.S. school. Honors both the student and the nominator.

scholarships.name: Minnesota State Fair Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awards for Minnesota residents entering any postsecondary year who have rural residency or an agriculture connection and plan to participate in the State Fair. Three additional 2,000 awards support skilled trade careers.

scholarships.name: Minnesota AFL-CIO Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Minnesota high school seniors graduating in the current year, with preference tied to union-family involvement and labor-history knowledge. Statewide competitive award.

scholarships.name: Minnesota FFA Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: A portfolio of scholarships for Minnesota FFA members pursuing postsecondary agriculture and related studies, including named funds such as the James W. Tracy and Thiher Family scholarships.

scholarships.name: Minnesota Elks Association Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships administered through local Minnesota Elks lodges for graduating high school seniors, in addition to the national Elks Most Valuable Student program. Applications go to the local lodge.

scholarships.name: VFW Voice of Democracy (Minnesota)
scholarships.description: Audio-essay competition for Minnesota students in grades 9 to 12 who submit a recorded patriotic-themed essay to a local VFW post, advancing to district, state, and national levels.

scholarships.name: VFW Patriot Pen (Minnesota)
scholarships.description: Written essay competition for Minnesota students in grades 6 to 8 on a patriotic theme, submitted to a local VFW post and advancing through district and state levels.

scholarships.name: Marshall H. and Nellie Alworth Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarships for northeastern Minnesota high school seniors pursuing degrees in the sciences, mathematics, and engineering fields. Awarded to students from the region planning STEM study.

scholarships.name: Minnesota Credit Union Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for members of Minnesota Credit Union Network affiliated credit unions who are high school seniors or students pursuing postsecondary education. Administered by the Foundation Scholarship Council.

scholarships.name: College Possible Minnesota Scholarship
scholarships.description: Non-renewable award of up to 5,000 for current college students with at least 12 earned credits from a bachelor's-granting institution, administered by The Minneapolis Foundation.

scholarships.name: North St. Paul-Maplewood-Oakdale Rotary Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Rotary Club of North St. Paul-Maplewood-Oakdale
scholarships.description: Scholarships including the Jack Hillstrom/William Woodworth and Jack Conzemius Memorial awards for graduating seniors in the ISD 622 community, paid over two years.

scholarships.name: Rotary Club of Lakeville STRIVE Scholarship
scholarships.description: STRIVE (Students Taking Renewed Interest in the Value of Education) scholarships of 1,000 for Lakeville high school seniors, presented at school awards nights in the spring.

scholarships.name: Charles R. Brett IBEW Minnesota State Council Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for children of IBEW members in Minnesota who are graduating high school seniors pursuing postsecondary education. Administered by the IBEW Minnesota State Council.

scholarships.name: SEIU Healthcare Minnesota Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for SEIU Healthcare Minnesota members and their dependents pursuing higher education, supporting healthcare and other fields of study.

scholarships.name: University of Minnesota U Promise Scholarship and Promise Plus Free Tuition
scholarships.description: Free-tuition program for Minnesota resident undergraduates whose families earn 50,000 dollars or less, covering remaining tuition after other aid at University of Minnesota campuses. No separate application beyond admission and the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: University of Minnesota System Promise Programs
scholarships.description: System-wide free and reduced tuition programs for Minnesota residents across University of Minnesota campuses, layering federal, state, and university aid for eligible income levels.

scholarships.name: Wells Fargo American Indian Studies Scholarship (UMD)
scholarships.description: Ten scholarships of 2,500 for University of Minnesota Duluth students connected to American Indian Studies, distributed across fall and spring semesters.

scholarships.name: Hmong American Education Fund Scholarships
scholarships.description: A portfolio of named scholarships for Hmong and Southeast Asian students in Minnesota, awarded annually to high school seniors and college students pursuing postsecondary education.

scholarships.name: United Hmong Education Foundation Academic Scholarship
scholarships.description: Academic scholarships for Hmong students in Minnesota pursuing higher education, disbursed upon proof of enrollment at an accredited institution.

scholarships.name: United Hmong American Association Scholarship
scholarships.description: Community scholarships for Hmong American students pursuing postsecondary education, awarded to graduating seniors and college students.

scholarships.name: UMN AANAPISI Scholarship
scholarships.organization: University of Minnesota Asian Pacific American Resource Center
scholarships.description: Scholarship supporting Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander students at the University of Minnesota through the AANAPISI initiative and Asian Pacific American Resource Center.

scholarships.name: Bright Flight Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.description: Merit award for top-scoring Missouri high school graduates who enroll full time at a participating Missouri college. Students scoring 32 or higher on the ACT qualify for up to $3,000; a 31 qualifies for up to $1,000. Must be a Missouri resident and US citizen or permanent resident.

scholarships.name: Access Missouri Financial Assistance Program
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.description: Need-based state grant for Missouri residents enrolled full time in undergraduate study at participating schools. Awards run from $500 to $1,700 at two-year schools and $1,750 to $3,500 at public four-year schools. Requires a FAFSA and a Student Aid Index of $12,000 or less.

scholarships.name: A+ Scholarship Program
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.amountLabel: Tuition and fees at MO community and technical colleges
scholarships.description: Covers unpaid tuition and general fees at participating Missouri community colleges and vocational schools for graduates of A+ designated high schools. Requires a 2.5 unweighted GPA, at least 95 percent attendance in grades 9 to 12, and 50 hours of unpaid tutoring or mentoring.

scholarships.name: Fast Track Workforce Incentive Grant
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.amountLabel: Tuition and fees not covered by other aid
scholarships.description: State grant for adult learners age 25 and older or independent students returning to school in a high-demand field. Covers tuition and fees remaining after other financial aid for eligible credit programs, workforce training, and apprenticeships in Missouri.

scholarships.name: Advanced Placement Incentive Grant
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.description: One-time grant for Missouri students who scored 3 or higher on qualifying Advanced Placement math or science exams in high school and enroll full time at a Missouri college pursuing a STEM field. Requires a FAFSA and Missouri residency.

scholarships.name: Marguerite Ross Barnett Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to part-time tuition at Mizzou rate
scholarships.description: Need-based award for Missouri students employed at least 20 hours per week who enroll at least half time but less than full time at a participating Missouri school. Applicants must be at least 18, demonstrate financial need, and be a Missouri resident.

scholarships.name: Dual Credit and Dual Enrollment Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.description: Helps Missouri high school students with financial need pay for approved dual credit or dual enrollment coursework taken through a participating Missouri college. Priority goes to students who qualify for free or reduced price lunch and to underrepresented students.

scholarships.name: Minority and Underrepresented Environmental Literacy Program (MUELP)
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.description: Supports minority and underrepresented Missouri students who pursue environmental studies at a participating Missouri college. Recipients agree to seek employment with the Missouri Department of Natural Resources after graduation.

scholarships.name: Minority Teaching Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Elementary and Secondary Education
scholarships.description: Competitive renewable award for minority Missouri students who commit to a teacher education program at a Missouri college. Applicants must rank in the top 25 percent of their high school class and score in the top 25 percent on the ACT or SAT. Recipients agree to teach in a Missouri public school after graduation.

scholarships.name: Wartime Veteran's Survivors Grant
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.description: Grant for children and spouses of Missouri veterans who died or became disabled as a result of service in a combat zone since September 11, 2001. Covers tuition at a rate not to exceed the University of Missouri rate for Missouri residents.

scholarships.name: CFO Universal Scholarship Application
scholarships.description: One application matches students across central and southern Missouri with hundreds of scholarship endowments held by the foundation and its regional affiliates. Opportunities cover graduating seniors, current undergraduates, and technical or graduate students, with many renewable for two to four years.

scholarships.name: Greater Kansas City Community Foundation Scholarships
