scholarships.description: The foundation administers more than 270 scholarship funds providing over $3 million a year to students in the Greater Kansas City metro pursuing two-year, four-year, trade, or postsecondary programs. A single general application matches students to the funds they qualify for.

scholarships.name: Scholarship Foundation of St. Louis Grants and Interest-Free Loans
scholarships.organization: The Scholarship Foundation of St. Louis
scholarships.description: Supports more than 500 students a year with grants and renewable interest-free loans based on academic potential, character, and significant financial need. Open to permanent residents of the St. Louis service area attending accredited nonprofit institutions for technical, associate, or bachelor's programs.

scholarships.name: St. Louis Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: The foundation runs about 80 scholarship programs that awarded over $2.5 million to more than 700 students in a recent year. Most opportunities are accessed through My Scholarship Central, a regional hub of private scholarship and interest-free loan programs for St. Louis area and Missouri students.

scholarships.name: Hispanic Development Fund Scholarship (High School Seniors)
scholarships.organization: Hispanic Development Fund via Greater Kansas City Community Foundation
scholarships.description: For Hispanic or Latinx high school seniors who graduate from a Greater Kansas City metro high school and enroll full time in an accredited college, trade, or certificate program. US citizenship is not required to apply. Reviewed on academic merit, financial need, and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Hispanic Development Fund Scholarship (Current College Students)
scholarships.organization: Hispanic Development Fund via Greater Kansas City Community Foundation
scholarships.description: For Hispanic or Latinx students who are already enrolled in an accredited college and are connected to the Greater Kansas City metro. Reviewed on academic merit, demonstrated financial need, and community involvement. US citizenship is not required to apply.

scholarships.name: Hispanic Educational, Cultural and Scholarship Fund
scholarships.organization: Hispanic Educational, Cultural and Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: Award for Hispanic or Latino students with a permanent home in the Greater St. Louis area who enroll in postsecondary coursework or trade school. At least one grandparent, living or deceased, must be of Hispanic or Latino heritage.

scholarships.name: Hispanic Festival Inc. Scholarship
scholarships.description: For high school seniors or current college students in the St. Louis metro area who enroll full time for the coming school year. Supports Hispanic and Latino students pursuing higher education in the St. Louis region.

scholarships.name: Black Community Scholarship Fund
scholarships.organization: Black Community Fund of Greater Kansas City
scholarships.description: Provides scholarship support to Black students from the Greater Kansas City area seeking a college or university degree or accredited certificate. Open to graduating high school seniors, current college students, and adults seeking educational or career advancement in the six-county metro.

scholarships.name: 100 Black Men of Metropolitan St. Louis Scholarship
scholarships.organization: 100 Black Men of Metropolitan St. Louis
scholarships.description: Annual scholarship helping African American students in the St. Louis area pursue college or vocational education. Applicants submit an essay on a selected topic judged by a panel of community leaders. Applications open in February and close in March.

scholarships.name: Urban League of Metropolitan St. Louis Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Urban League of Metropolitan St. Louis
scholarships.description: College scholarships offered as part of the Urban League's educational excellence work to prepare students for economic self-reliance. Serves students across the St. Louis region.

scholarships.name: Show-Me to College Scholarship
scholarships.description: Private scholarship for Missouri high school seniors with a 3.50 GPA or higher and demonstrated financial need based on the FAFSA. Requires a record of community service, extracurricular participation, or work experience. Renewable for up to four years at an eligible Missouri institution.

scholarships.name: Missouri Farm Bureau Foundation for Agriculture Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Missouri Farm Bureau Foundation for Agriculture
scholarships.description: Awards to Missouri high school seniors entering a four-year college with a declared major in an agricultural field. The student, a parent, or guardian must hold a current Missouri Farm Bureau membership. Four scholarships are awarded each year.

scholarships.name: AGC of Missouri Education Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Associated General Contractors of Missouri Education Foundation
scholarships.description: Supports students pursuing a construction or construction-related field who attend or plan to attend a registered apprenticeship or certified program. Requires official transcripts and two letters of recommendation submitted through the foundation's application platform.

scholarships.name: Missouri REALTORS Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship support for those pursuing education in the real estate industry in Missouri. Applications are submitted through the Missouri REALTORS website.

scholarships.name: Mizzou Freshman Merit Scholarships
scholarships.description: Automatic merit awards for incoming Missouri resident freshmen based on the Mizzou core GPA and curriculum rigor. Tiers include the Excellence Award at $3,500, the Curators Scholars Award at $5,000, the Chancellor's Award at $7,200, and the Mizzou Scholars Award at $11,000 a year, renewable for four years.

scholarships.name: Truman State University TruMerit Scholarship
scholarships.description: Automatic merit scholarship for admitted freshmen based on GPA and verified test scores, awarded from $2,000 up to $10,000 a year. No separate application beyond admission is required.

scholarships.name: Missouri State University Presidential Scholarship
scholarships.description: Competitive freshman award for high-achieving incoming students with a 31 ACT or 1390 SAT and a 3.90 cumulative GPA at the sixth semester. Test scores must be from tests taken by October of senior year.

scholarships.name: University of Central Missouri Undergraduate Scholarships
scholarships.description: Merit and program scholarships for incoming and continuing undergraduates at UCM in Warrensburg. Many freshman awards are based on GPA and test scores through the admission application.

scholarships.name: UMSL Scholarships for Hispanic and Latino Students
scholarships.description: A group of scholarship opportunities at the University of Missouri-St. Louis directed to Hispanic and Latino students, matched through the university's scholarship portal.

scholarships.name: Missouri 4-H Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: A set of scholarships for active Missouri 4-H members pursuing higher education, recognizing project work, leadership, and community service. Multiple named awards are offered through the Missouri 4-H Foundation.

scholarships.name: My Scholarship Central Regional Scholarships
scholarships.organization: St. Louis Graduates / My Scholarship Central
scholarships.description: A regional hub of more than 130 private scholarship and interest-free loan programs for students in the St. Louis region and across Missouri. One general application matches students to programs they qualify for.

scholarships.name: Kids' Chance of Missouri Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development / Kids' Chance
scholarships.description: Assists Missouri students whose parent was seriously injured or killed in a work-related accident covered by workers' compensation. Helps cover the cost of postsecondary education for eligible dependent children.

scholarships.name: Public Service Officer Survivor Grant
scholarships.organization: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
scholarships.description: Grant for children and spouses of Missouri public safety officers and Department of Transportation employees who were killed or permanently and totally disabled in the line of duty. Covers tuition and fees at participating Missouri schools.

scholarships.name: Palmetto Fellows Scholarship
scholarships.organization: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to $6,700 freshman year, up to $7,500 upper years
scholarships.description: Merit award for the most academically talented South Carolina high school seniors who attend an eligible in-state college. Requires strong GPA plus SAT/ACT and class rank. Renewable with a 3.0 GPA and 30 credit hours per year.

scholarships.name: LIFE Scholarship
scholarships.organization: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to $5,000/yr (up to $7,500 with STEM/education enhancement)
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship for South Carolina residents attending in-state colleges, awarded automatically based on the high school record. Requires meeting two of three criteria: 3.0 GPA, 1100 SAT or 24 ACT, top 30 percent class rank. Renewable with a 3.0 college GPA.

scholarships.name: SC HOPE Scholarship
scholarships.organization: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship for South Carolina high school seniors entering a four-year institution who do not qualify for the LIFE or Palmetto Fellows scholarships. Awarded for the freshman year only, based on a 3.0 high school GPA.

scholarships.name: South Carolina Need-based Grant
scholarships.organization: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for South Carolina residents attending eligible in-state public and independent colleges. Eligibility is determined from the FAFSA, and part-time students may receive up to $1,750 per year.

scholarships.name: South Carolina Tuition Grants
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for South Carolina residents attending an eligible independent (private) college in the state. Award size depends on family income, assets, family size and cost of attendance, and requires the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Lottery Tuition Assistance Program
scholarships.organization: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
scholarships.description: Assistance for South Carolina residents enrolled at a state two-year community or technical college. Full-time students may receive up to $1,140 per term and awards factor in academic progress and financial need.

scholarships.name: South Carolina Teaching Fellows Program
scholarships.organization: South Carolina Center for Educator Recruitment, Retention, and Advancement (CERRA)
scholarships.description: Fellowship for South Carolina high school seniors who plan to become teachers, selecting up to 230 students each year based on academics, community service and commitment to teaching. Fellows attend a partner SC college and complete an enrichment program.

scholarships.name: SC WINS Scholarship
scholarships.organization: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
scholarships.description: Workforce Industry Needs Scholarship for South Carolina technical college students pursuing programs in high-demand fields. It supplements Lottery Tuition Assistance to help cover tuition, fees and books for eligible workforce programs.

scholarships.name: SC National Guard College Assistance Program
scholarships.organization: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
scholarships.description: Tuition assistance for active members of the South Carolina Army and Air National Guard attending eligible in-state colleges. Members may receive up to $12,000 per academic year toward tuition and fees.

scholarships.name: A.C. Flora Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for graduating seniors at A.C. Flora High School in Columbia who show involvement in extracurricular activities and demonstrated financial need. Requires a minimum 2.75 GPA.

scholarships.name: Alpha Iota Boule - Matthew J. Perry, Jr. Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable award for current or incoming law students at ABA-accredited institutions in South Carolina, with financial need and leadership qualities. Preference is given to African American students from South Carolina.

scholarships.name: Benny and Eleanor Clark Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable award for South Carolina residents attending an HBCU in the state, or for African American employees and dependents of SC McDonald's franchises. Requires a minimum 2.0 GPA.

scholarships.name: Bertha and Addison Bostain, Sr. Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable award for Chapin, South Carolina high school graduates entering college as freshmen, with a minimum 2.5 GPA. Preference is given to African American students.

scholarships.name: Bobbi Rossi Memorial Scholarship (Cardinal Newman School)
scholarships.description: Award for current juniors at Cardinal Newman School in Columbia who maintain high moral standards and a minimum 2.5 GPA. Applied toward college costs.

scholarships.name: Bobbi Rossi Memorial Scholarship (USC School of Nursing)
scholarships.description: Renewable award for junior and senior nursing students at the University of South Carolina in Columbia with a minimum 3.0 GPA.

scholarships.name: Central Carolina Community Foundation Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable award for first-generation college students who are high school seniors or undergraduates in the Foundation's 11-county service area, with demonstrated community involvement.

scholarships.name: Dinkins Family Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable award for high school seniors in the Foundation's 11-county service area attending a four-year public university in South Carolina, with priority for first-generation students.

scholarships.name: Dr. Robert Howard/WHS Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Orangeburg-Wilkinson High School seniors with a minimum 3.0 GPA and demonstrated financial need. Preference for students attending South Carolina State University or Claflin University.

scholarships.name: Grace Brooks and E. Perry Palmer (Claflin) Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for African American high school students in the Foundation's 11-county service area pursuing philosophy and religion degrees at Claflin University.

scholarships.name: Zack and Rachel Clarkson Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Lower Richland High School seniors in Columbia, with special consideration for African American males who demonstrate financial need.

scholarships.name: Amanda's Scholarship Fund
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Renewable annual award of $5,000 for a student from Berkeley, Charleston or Dorchester county in the South Carolina Lowcountry.

scholarships.name: Rufus C. Barkley, Jr. Leadership Scholarship Fund
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Renewable annual award of $10,000 for high school seniors in the Lowcountry selected on academic merit and character.

scholarships.name: Warren O. Pinckney Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Award of $500 to $2,000 for students in the Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester county region of coastal South Carolina.

scholarships.name: J.C. and Alberta Long Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Award of up to $2,000 for students from the Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester county region of South Carolina.

scholarships.name: William Melvin and Juanita W. Brown Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Award of up to $2,000 for students in the Lowcountry region of coastal South Carolina.

scholarships.name: Mother Emanuel A.M.E. Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Award of up to $5,600 established in memory of the Mother Emanuel A.M.E. Church in Charleston, supporting Lowcountry students pursuing higher education.

scholarships.name: Porgy & Bess Music Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Award of $1,000 to $2,000 for Lowcountry students pursuing the study of music.

scholarships.name: Hebrew Orphan Society N. Edgar Miles, M.D. Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Award of up to $2,000 for students in the coastal South Carolina region, administered through the Hebrew Orphan Society fund.

scholarships.name: UPLIFT Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Award of up to $5,000 supporting students from the Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester county region of South Carolina.

scholarships.name: Faith Jefferson Hohloch Nursing Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Award for students from Berkeley, Charleston or Dorchester county working toward a baccalaureate or higher degree in nursing.

scholarships.name: Charleston First Responders Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
scholarships.description: Award for Charleston-area first responders and their children or spouses who are college-bound or currently enrolled in college.

scholarships.name: Bud and Billie Eubanks Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for Batesburg-Leesville High School seniors attending Clemson University who demonstrate financial need, paying up to $20,000 across four years.

scholarships.name: Ride of Your Life Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for South Carolina high school seniors pursuing any certification or degree, judged on communication skills and academics.

scholarships.name: Dr. Doretha Pressey Academic Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Dr. Doretha Pressey Southern Scholars Initiative
scholarships.description: Award for graduating seniors from Bamberg County, South Carolina high schools who are of African, Indigenous, Asian or Hispanic descent, pursuing a four-year degree.

scholarships.name: Mrs. Clara Mae Coleman Technical School Award
scholarships.organization: Dr. Doretha Pressey Southern Scholars Initiative
scholarships.description: Award for graduating seniors from Bamberg County, South Carolina high schools of African, Indigenous, Asian or Hispanic descent who plan to attend a technical school.

scholarships.name: Sunshine Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for high school seniors from Florence and Marion, South Carolina who have a 3.0 or higher GPA, financial need and a history of overcoming obstacles.

scholarships.name: Horatio Alger South Carolina Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for South Carolina high school seniors who have faced and overcome significant adversity, demonstrate critical financial need (family income generally under $100,000) and are committed to completing a college degree.

scholarships.name: Stamps Scholars Award (University of South Carolina)
scholarships.organization: University of South Carolina / Stamps Scholars
scholarships.description: Prestigious merit award for incoming University of South Carolina undergraduates, covering enrichment funding on top of other aid for academically exceptional students.

scholarships.name: AHAM Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for high school seniors of Hispanic origin or descent enrolled in a public or private high school in one of ten Upstate South Carolina counties. Requires a minimum 3.5 GPA and family income not exceeding $70,000.

scholarships.name: Advocates for African Americans Carolinas Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for high school seniors pursuing studies at universities in North or South Carolina, supporting African American students in the Carolinas.

scholarships.name: South Carolina Farm Bureau Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: South Carolina Farm Bureau Federation Educational Foundation
scholarships.description: Award honoring past South Carolina Farm Bureau leaders, supporting SC students pursuing agriculture-related fields of study.

scholarships.name: Wisconsin Grant (UW, Technical and Tribal Colleges)
scholarships.amountLabel: Varies by financial need and enrollment
scholarships.description: Grant assistance for Wisconsin resident undergraduates enrolled at least part time at UW System, Wisconsin technical, or tribal colleges. Awards are based on financial need, prorated by enrollment level, and cannot exceed ten semesters. Students qualify by filing the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Wisconsin Grant (Private Nonprofit Colleges)
scholarships.amountLabel: Varies by financial need and enrollment
scholarships.description: Need based grant for Wisconsin residents attending independent, nonprofit colleges and universities in Wisconsin. Enrollment must be at least part time, with a ten semester lifetime limit, and awards are prorated by enrollment. Eligibility is determined through the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Talent Incentive Program (TIP) Grant
scholarships.description: Grant for the most financially needy and educationally disadvantaged Wisconsin resident students. First time freshmen must be nominated by a college financial aid office or a Wisconsin Educational Opportunity Programs counselor. Students attend Wisconsin colleges at least half time.

scholarships.name: Academic Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship for the Wisconsin high school seniors with the highest grade point average at their school. Each eligible high school nominates students, and the number of scholars depends on enrollment size. Recipients must enroll full time at a participating Wisconsin college by September 30.

scholarships.name: Wisconsin Tuition Promise
scholarships.amountLabel: Covers remaining tuition and fees (last dollar)
scholarships.description: Free tuition and segregated fees for new first year and transfer students whose family adjusted gross income is at or below $55,000, at participating UW System universities other than UW Madison. Students file the FAFSA, enroll full time, and stay continuously enrolled while meeting academic progress standards.

scholarships.name: Bucky's Tuition Promise
scholarships.amountLabel: Full tuition and segregated fees (last dollar)
scholarships.description: Guarantees scholarships and grants to cover tuition and segregated fees for incoming Wisconsin resident students whose family adjusted gross income is $65,000 or less. First year students receive up to four years and transfer students up to two years. Applicants submit the CSS Profile for the incoming year and the FAFSA yearly.

scholarships.name: Herb Kohl Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.description: Recognizes Wisconsin high school seniors for leadership, citizenship, school and community involvement, and academic achievement. The foundation awards 100 scholarships each year to students in public, private, and homeschool settings who plan to attend a two or four year college. Students apply through the SmartSimple platform.

scholarships.name: Herb Kohl Student Initiative Scholarship
scholarships.description: Honors Wisconsin high school students who have demonstrated strong promise despite facing significant obstacles or personal adversity. Selection weighs perseverance, leadership, and the ability to overcome challenges rather than grade point average alone. Students apply through the same foundation platform as the Excellence award.

scholarships.name: Milwaukee's Finest Scholarship
scholarships.description: Supports graduating seniors from a Milwaukee County high school who have four years of county attendance and plan to enroll in an associate or bachelor's degree program. Applicants show leadership through community service and extracurricular activities and must demonstrate financial need with one letter of recommendation.

scholarships.name: Hmong Community Higher Education Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Community Foundation of North Central Wisconsin
scholarships.description: Awards students of Hmong descent from the central Wisconsin area who are pursuing a college degree in any field. Two awards go to graduating high school seniors and two to current undergraduate students at accredited colleges. The fund encourages recipients to return to the area in professional and leadership roles.

scholarships.name: WHSF Mexican Fiesta Scholarship
scholarships.description: Open to Wisconsin residents of at least 25 percent Hispanic descent who are entering or enrolled full time at a Wisconsin two or four year college, university, or graduate school. Applicants need a grade point average of 2.5 or higher and complete at least 20 volunteer hours during the Mexican Fiesta festival in Milwaukee.

scholarships.name: Hispanic Professionals of Greater Milwaukee Scholarship
scholarships.description: Supports Latino students in Wisconsin pursuing higher education, part of a scholarship program that has awarded more than one million dollars since 2001. The organization connects students to education, mentorship, and professional development across an ecosystem of corporate and community partners.

scholarships.name: Educators Credit Union Scholarship
scholarships.description: Offered to graduating high school seniors who are primary owners of an active savings account at Educators Credit Union for at least one year and attend high school in one of eleven southeastern Wisconsin counties. Applicants write a short essay reflecting the credit union's core values and plan to attend college or technical school.

scholarships.name: WESTconsin Credit Union Student Scholarship
scholarships.description: Available to graduating high school seniors who are members of WESTconsin Credit Union in western Wisconsin. The program awards up to thirty scholarships of $500 each to students continuing their education. Applications and instructions are posted on the credit union website.

scholarships.name: Wisconsin American Legion Auxiliary Van Deuren Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.organization: American Legion Auxiliary Department of Wisconsin
scholarships.description: Awarded to a Wisconsin student whose mother or self is a member of a Wisconsin American Legion Auxiliary unit. Applicants must be Wisconsin residents with at least a 3.5 grade point average, and the application must be signed by a sponsoring local Auxiliary unit.

scholarships.name: Schneider-Emanuel American Legion Scholarship
scholarships.description: Provides three awards of $1,000 to Wisconsin high school graduates. The scholarship recognizes students continuing to college and is administered by the American Legion Department of Wisconsin as part of its youth programs.

scholarships.name: American Legion Wisconsin Eagle Scout of the Year Scholarship
scholarships.description: Recognizes an outstanding Eagle Scout connected to the American Legion in Wisconsin. The award totals $10,000 distributed across four years of postsecondary study, with a March 1 application deadline through the Department of Wisconsin.

scholarships.name: Wisconsin FFA Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Provides scholarships to Wisconsin FFA members who are graduating high school seniors or current college students in good standing with the Wisconsin Association of FFA. Selection weighs academic achievement, leadership, supervised agricultural experience, recommendations, and personal circumstances. Many awards support students pursuing agriculture related fields.

scholarships.name: American Indian Chamber of Commerce of Wisconsin Scholarship
scholarships.organization: American Indian Chamber of Commerce of Wisconsin
scholarships.description: Awards American Indian or Alaska Native Wisconsin residents pursuing a bachelor's, graduate, or doctoral degree. Applicants need a grade point average of 3.0 or higher, an essay, and evidence of community service, extracurricular activities, or work. Both financial need and academic merit are considered.

scholarships.name: Wisconsin Indian Education Association Scholarship
scholarships.description: Provides scholarship assistance to American Indian students from Wisconsin attending institutions of higher education. The award is achievement based rather than need based and recognizes academic accomplishment among Native students across the state.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation for the Fox Valley Region Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Community Foundation for the Fox Valley Region
scholarships.description: A single application connects Fox Valley area students to hundreds of community funded scholarships worth more than two million dollars. Awards serve high school seniors, college undergraduates, graduate students, and trade students from Appleton, Oshkosh, Neenah, Menasha, and surrounding Wisconsin communities.

scholarships.name: Oshkosh Area Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: One comprehensive application through the Fox River Scholarship Center connects graduating high school seniors in Green Lake, Waushara, and Winnebago counties to multiple scholarship funds. The foundation partners with area districts including Oshkosh, Neenah, Omro, Princeton, Ripon, Wautoma, and Winneconne.

scholarships.name: La Crosse Area Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Administers more than fifty scholarship funds awarding over 250,000 dollars each year to area students. High school seniors apply through their school guidance office, while college and nontraditional students apply through their financial aid office at Western Technical College, Viterbo University, or UW La Crosse.

scholarships.name: Racine Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Manages more than forty scholarship funds established by community members, each tied to a specific Racine area high school or university. The foundation publishes an index listing each school, the number of scholarships available, and the individual fund names.

scholarships.name: Green Bay Packers Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Supports graduating high school seniors from Brown County who participate in sports, maintain a grade point average above 3.2, show community involvement, and demonstrate financial need. Awards are administered through Scholarships Inc. for four year college students and NWTC for two year and trade students.

scholarships.name: MPS Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Offers more than thirty scholarship opportunities exclusively for graduating Milwaukee Public Schools seniors. A single online application screens students and guides them to the awards they qualify for based on background, academics, and college plans. Many recipients are first generation students and students of color.

scholarships.name: Wisconsin Restaurant Association Education Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awards Wisconsin residents enrolled in at least six credits at an accredited postsecondary school in culinary, baking, hospitality, food science, or family and consumer science education. Selection is based on future plans in foodservice, academic records, and recommendations, with checks issued to the school in two installments.

scholarships.name: Engineers Foundation of Wisconsin Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awards graduating Wisconsin high school seniors who plan to study engineering at a four year ABET accredited program and intend to enter the engineering profession. Applicants need an ACT composite of 26 or higher and a grade point average of 3.2 or higher. Named awards include the Louis C. Geiger and Robert G. Cooper scholarships.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of North Central Wisconsin Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Community Foundation of North Central Wisconsin
scholarships.description: A universal application matches students to scholarship funds serving the Greater Wausau area, Marathon County, and Langlade, Lincoln, Oneida, and Taylor counties, plus statewide Wisconsin awards. Eligibility differs by fund and can include academics, service, field of study, financial need, and cultural background.

scholarships.name: Marshfield Area Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: A single online portal application connects graduating high school seniors and returning students from the Marshfield service area to seventy nine scholarship funds, plus several specialized awards. Donor determined criteria filter applicants to the funds they qualify for.

scholarships.name: Kiwanis Club of West Racine Scholarship
scholarships.description: Offered by the Kiwanis Club of West Racine to graduating high school students in the Racine area who plan to continue their education. The club opens applications early in the year and recognizes students for academics, service, and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Wisconsin American Legion Auxiliary Department President's Scholarship
scholarships.organization: American Legion Auxiliary Department of Wisconsin
scholarships.description: Offers three scholarships to attend a college or university of the applicant's choice. Either the applicant or the applicant's mother must be a member of a Wisconsin American Legion Auxiliary unit, and applicants are Wisconsin residents with strong academic records.

scholarships.name: WESTconsin Credit Union and Regional Community Awards (Fort Community Credit Union Scholarship)
scholarships.description: Fort Community Credit Union offers scholarships to student members in the Fort Atkinson, Jefferson, Whitewater, and Watertown areas of Wisconsin who are continuing their education. Awards recognize members for academics and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Roberta B. Willis Scholarship - Need-Based Grant
scholarships.description: State need-based grant for Connecticut residents attending eligible in-state public or nonprofit colleges. Awarded based on financial need determined by the FAFSA. Students should file the FAFSA and complete their college enrollment; no separate application is required.

scholarships.name: Roberta B. Willis Scholarship - Need-Merit Award
scholarships.description: State need-merit award for high-achieving Connecticut high school seniors ranking in the top 20 percent of their class or scoring at least 1200 SAT (or 25 ACT), who also meet a Student Aid Index cutoff. Recipients must attend a Connecticut public or nonprofit college. The high school counselor submits nominations.

scholarships.name: Hartford Foundation for Public Giving Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: A single universal application connects Greater Hartford students to hundreds of donor-established scholarship funds for four-year, two-year, graduate, vocational, and adult learners. Awards vary by fund and cover schools in Connecticut and nationwide.

scholarships.name: Fairfield County's Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 100 scholarship funds administered through one online application for residents of Fairfield County or graduates of a Fairfield County high school. Open to graduating seniors, undergraduates, graduate, non-traditional, and vocational or technical students.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation for Greater New Haven Scholarships
scholarships.organization: The Community Foundation for Greater New Haven
scholarships.description: The Foundation administers scholarship funds for students in the Greater New Haven area, awarded through partner schools and organizations. Applicants must generally be Connecticut residents enrolled in or admitted to an accredited postsecondary program.

scholarships.name: New Haven Promise Scholarship
scholarships.description: Place-based scholarship for students who live in New Haven and attend New Haven public schools, earn a 3.0 GPA, maintain 90 percent attendance, and demonstrate good behavior. Covers up to full tuition at Connecticut public colleges and up to $2,500 at in-state private nonprofit colleges.

scholarships.name: Milton Fisher Scholarship for Innovation and Creativity
scholarships.description: Rewards high school seniors and first-time college freshmen who show innovative and creative problem-solving. Open to students who live in Connecticut or the New York City metro area attending college anywhere in the US, or students anywhere in the US attending college in Connecticut or the NYC metro. Renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Connecticut Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 140 scholarship funds for students from Greater Waterbury and the Litchfield Hills, open to high school seniors, current college students, and adult learners in undergraduate, graduate, or vocational programs. Awards are based on need, academics, major, community involvement, or donor criteria.

scholarships.name: Main Street Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: About 100 donor-established scholarship funds for residents of Bristol, Burlington, Plainville, Plymouth, Southington, and Wolcott. Applied for through one online application supporting students from secondary school through college and career training.

scholarships.name: CALAHE Competitive Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Connecticut Association of Latinos in Higher Education
scholarships.description: Awarded to Latino high school seniors and undergraduates who have been Connecticut residents for at least twelve months, are seeking a first undergraduate degree, and have demonstrated community service within the Latino community. Selection considers academics, financial need, service, and an essay.

scholarships.name: Connecticut Building Congress Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For graduating Connecticut high school seniors entering college programs in architecture, construction-related engineering, construction management, surveying, or planning. Awards are based on academic merit, extracurriculars, potential, and financial need; about 20 recipients funded annually.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Eastern Connecticut Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 150 donor-established scholarship funds for residents of eastern Connecticut, spanning high school seniors, current and returning college students, and graduate students across many fields. Applied for through the Foundation's online scholarship portal.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Greater New Britain Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Community Foundation of Greater New Britain
scholarships.description: More than seventy scholarship funds for residents of Berlin, New Britain, Plainville, and Southington, published each year in the Foundation's scholarship directory. Over $270,000 awarded annually through one online application portal.

scholarships.name: Big Y Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Merit-based scholarships for students who live in Connecticut or Massachusetts or attend a school in those states, including graduating high school seniors, undergraduates, and graduate students. Employees, dependents, and customers are encouraged to apply through the online system.

scholarships.name: American Savings Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need-based scholarships for about 100 students living in the 64 Connecticut towns served by the Foundation. Open to high school seniors, current college students, and nontraditional adult students who have not completed a bachelor's degree. No minimum GPA required.

scholarships.name: Stephen Phillips Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable need-based scholarship for full-time undergraduates who are permanent residents of Connecticut or another New England state, pursuing a bachelor's degree. Requires an SAI of 13,000 or less and unmet need of at least $7,000. Reviewed for service, work ethic, and leadership.

scholarships.name: Liberty Bank Kindness Scholarship
scholarships.description: Statewide Connecticut scholarship recognizing students who demonstrate kindness and community impact. Awarded through the Liberty Bank community program.

scholarships.name: Bohdan Kolinsky Memorial Sports Media Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Connecticut students pursuing a career in sports journalism or sports media. Awarded by the Connecticut Sports Writers organization.

scholarships.name: SWE Hartford Section Freshman Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Society of Women Engineers, Hartford Section
scholarships.description: For women entering an ABET-accredited engineering or computer science program at a college in the Connecticut area. Supports first-year students beginning their engineering studies.

scholarships.name: SWE Connecticut Jean R. Beers Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Society of Women Engineers, Connecticut Section
scholarships.description: Scholarship for women pursuing STEM degrees who are Connecticut residents or students. Awarded by the Connecticut section of the Society of Women Engineers.

scholarships.name: CHESLA Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Connecticut Higher Education Supplemental Loan Authority
scholarships.description: Need-based scholarship for Connecticut residents enrolled at least half-time who are Pell Grant eligible with a minimum 2.5 GPA. Awards are up to $1,500 for half-time and up to $3,000 for full-time students, first-come first-served until funds run out.

scholarships.name: Waterbury Promise Scholarship
scholarships.description: Place-based last-dollar scholarship for graduates of Waterbury schools meeting GPA, attendance, and residency requirements. Provides up to $5,000 per year toward college, up to $20,000 over four years.

scholarships.name: UConn Nutmeg Scholarship
scholarships.description: Full merit scholarship for exceptional Connecticut secondary school seniors admitted to the Storrs campus, limited to about 20 recipients statewide. Requires Connecticut residency, exceptional academics, notable service, and leadership. Admission application due Nov 1, Nutmeg supplement due Nov 8.

scholarships.name: UConn Day of Pride Scholarship
scholarships.description: Full cost-of-attendance scholarship for outstanding incoming students from underserved backgrounds, including Connecticut residents. Requires a supplemental application in addition to the admissions application.

scholarships.name: UConn Presidential Scholars Award
scholarships.amountLabel: Full tuition, fees, room and board
scholarships.description: Prestigious award covering full tuition, fees, room, and board for the four-year undergraduate career at UConn. Considered for students ranking first or second in their high school graduating class, including Connecticut residents. Automatic consideration with the admissions application.

scholarships.name: Hartford Promise Scholarship
scholarships.description: Place-based scholarship for graduates of Hartford public schools who meet residency, GPA, and attendance requirements. Provides up to $5,000 per year toward college, and pairs with the Greater Futures program for additional support.

scholarships.name: Minority Teacher Incentive Program (MTIP)
scholarships.description: Grant for Connecticut students in teacher-preparation programs who commit to teaching in a Connecticut public school. Provides up to $5,000 per year in junior and senior years, plus up to $2,500 per year in student loan reimbursement for up to four years of teaching. Nominated by the education dean.

scholarships.name: Stanley Black & Decker Scholars of Excellence
scholarships.organization: University of Hartford / Stanley Black & Decker
scholarships.description: Scholarship funded by a gift from Stanley Black & Decker for top academically prepared students from 29 Greater Hartford towns who enroll at the University of Hartford. Recipients gain mentoring, resume workshops, and leadership development with company employees.

scholarships.name: Norwalk Community College Foundation Path2Success Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship support for students at the Norwalk campus of CT State Community College. Awarded through the Norwalk Community College Foundation to help cover tuition and educational costs.

scholarships.name: Eastern Connecticut State University Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Institutional scholarship funds for admitted and current Eastern Connecticut State University students, matched through the FAFSA and departmental input. Filing the FAFSA by the priority date maximizes consideration.

scholarships.name: Robert T. Kenney Scholarship (American Savings Foundation)
scholarships.description: Named scholarship track within the American Savings Foundation program for students in the Foundation's central Connecticut service area, emphasizing financial need and community involvement. Renewable for students who maintain eligibility.

scholarships.name: Bridgeport Public Education Fund Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships administered by the Bridgeport Public Education Fund for graduates of Bridgeport Public Schools who meet GPA, attendance, and residency requirements. Supports local students transitioning to college.

scholarships.name: CTCPA Accounting Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Connecticut residents pursuing accounting degrees and a CPA career path, awarded by the Connecticut Society of Certified Public Accountants.

scholarships.name: Middlesex Community College Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Foundation scholarship funds for students at the Middlesex campus of CT State Community College, covering a range of donor criteria and fields of study. Applied for through the campus foundation scholarship cycle.

scholarships.name: All Iowa Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Iowa Department of Education (Iowa College Aid)
scholarships.description: State scholarship for Iowa high school graduates who are first-time college freshmen at an eligible Iowa college or university, based on financial need. Renewable for up to eight full-time semesters.

scholarships.name: Iowa Tuition Grant
scholarships.organization: Iowa Department of Education (Iowa College Aid)
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for Iowa residents enrolled at eligible Iowa private (not-for-profit) colleges and universities. Available for up to four years of full-time undergraduate study.

scholarships.name: Iowa Vocational-Technical Tuition Grant
scholarships.organization: Iowa Department of Education (Iowa College Aid)
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for Iowa residents enrolled in a vocational, technical or career-option program at an Iowa community college.

scholarships.name: Future Ready Iowa Last-Dollar Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Iowa Workforce Development / Iowa College Aid
scholarships.description: Covers tuition and qualified fees not paid by other federal and state aid for Iowa residents earning a certificate, diploma or associate degree in a high-demand career field at an Iowa community college.

scholarships.name: Iowa National Guard Service Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Iowa National Guard / Iowa College Aid
scholarships.description: Tuition assistance for members of the Iowa Army or Air National Guard pursuing an undergraduate degree at an eligible Iowa college or university. Award reduced by federal tuition assistance.

scholarships.name: Robert D. Blue Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Office of the State Treasurer of Iowa
scholarships.description: Awarded to Iowa residents attending an in-state college or university, judged on financial need, an original citizenship essay, academic achievement and two recommendation letters.

scholarships.name: Iowa Scholarship for the Arts
scholarships.organization: Iowa Arts Council (Iowa Economic Development Authority)
scholarships.description: For graduating Iowa high school seniors with proven artistic ability in music, dance, visual arts, theatre, folklife or literature who will major in the arts full-time at an Iowa college or university.

scholarships.name: Iowa Farm Bureau Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to 27 graduating Iowa high school seniors (three per district) whose family holds an active Iowa Farm Bureau membership. Renewable for four years.

scholarships.name: Iowa Pork Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Iowa Pork Producers Association / Iowa Pork Foundation
scholarships.description: For Iowa students majoring in an agriculture-related field with an emphasis on the swine industry at a two- or four-year college. Fifteen incoming and fifteen returning students awarded.

scholarships.name: Iowa Newspaper Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Iowa residents who are high school seniors or current college students planning careers in the newspaper industry in Iowa and attending an in-state college. Requires two references and two work samples.

scholarships.name: Iowa 4-H Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Over 90 scholarships for Iowa 4-H youth who are high school seniors or current college students. One application covers all awards; one scholarship per student per year.

scholarships.name: Iowa Bankers Association 4-H Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Iowa high school seniors who are Iowa 4-H members planning to attend an Iowa college, selected on academics, activities, leadership and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Iowa CPA Education Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Iowa college accounting students who commit to taking the CPA exam in Iowa. Applications open in January through the ISCPA faculty liaison at qualifying Iowa colleges.

scholarships.name: Iowa State Elks Association Vocational Grant
scholarships.description: Twenty grants for Iowa residents pursuing a two-year-or-less vocational or technical training program at an accredited school. Open to high school seniors and non-traditional students.

scholarships.name: Iowa Physician Assistant Society Scholarship
scholarships.description: One scholarship per Iowa PA program for students enrolled in an approved in-state Physician Assistant program, based on academics, leadership and professionalism.

scholarships.name: IHCA Foundation Nursing Scholarship (High School Seniors)
scholarships.description: Nine scholarships for Iowa high school seniors interested in pursuing a nursing career in long-term care.

scholarships.name: IHCA Foundation Long-Term Care Employee Scholarship
scholarships.description: Nine scholarships for employees at IHCA member organizations enrolled or accepted in an accredited long-term care degree program.

scholarships.name: LULAC National Scholarship Fund (Iowa Councils)
scholarships.organization: League of United Latin American Citizens (LNESC)
scholarships.description: For Hispanic students, including DACA recipients, applying to or enrolled at a college or vocational school. Local Iowa LULAC councils review applications on academics, need and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Iowa Scholars Award
scholarships.description: Automatic merit scholarship for admitted Iowa resident first-year students, based on academic merit. Renewable up to four years with a 2.75 UI GPA.

scholarships.name: University of Iowa Provost Scholarship
scholarships.description: For National Merit finalists who name the University of Iowa as their first choice. Renewable for up to four years.

scholarships.name: Iowa State University Loyal Scholar Award
scholarships.description: Automatic recognition award for admitted Iowa resident first-year students with a 3.80 GPA and ACT 32 / SAT 1450. Renewable four years with a 2.50 GPA.

scholarships.name: Iowa State University Forever Scholar Award
scholarships.description: Automatic recognition award for admitted Iowa resident first-year students with a 3.60 GPA and ACT 28 / SAT 1300. Renewable four years with a 2.50 GPA.

scholarships.name: Iowa State University True Scholar Award
scholarships.description: Automatic recognition award for admitted Iowa resident first-year students with a 4.00 GPA and no test score required. Renewable four years with a 2.50 GPA.

scholarships.name: UNI Presidential Scholarship
scholarships.description: Competitive scholarship for incoming freshmen with outstanding academics plus leadership and service. Stacks with the Panther Award for Iowa residents. Renewable four years with a 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: UNI Panther Award
scholarships.description: Automatic merit award for admitted Iowa resident freshmen based on GPA and/or ACT. Renewable four years with a 2.5 GPA; priority for students admitted by May 1.

scholarships.name: UNI Inspire Award
scholarships.description: Automatic award for admitted freshmen with a minimum 3.5 high school GPA and demonstrated financial need on the FAFSA. Renewable four years with a 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: Quad Cities Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 70 scholarships for students in the Quad Cities region, including Iowa's Cedar, Clinton, Des Moines, Henry, Jackson, Louisa, Muscatine and Scott counties. High school seniors, graduates of all ages and some graduate students may apply through one online application.

scholarships.name: Greater Cedar Rapids Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Multiple scholarships for eastern Iowa students, primarily Linn County, requiring full-time enrollment at an accredited nonprofit or public college. One online application matches students to eligible funds.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Greater Des Moines Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Community Foundation of Greater Des Moines
scholarships.description: Scholarship funds administered for central Iowa students, applied for through the foundation's online scholarship portal.

scholarships.name: Kibbie Grant (Skilled Workforce Shortage Tuition Grant)
scholarships.organization: Iowa Department of Education (Iowa College Aid)
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for Iowa residents enrolled in a career-technical or high-demand program at an Iowa community college. Awarded via the FAFSA and Iowa Financial Aid Application.

scholarships.name: Gap Tuition Assistance Program
scholarships.organization: Iowa Department of Education (Iowa College Aid)
scholarships.description: Need-based tuition assistance for Iowa adult learners enrolled in eligible continuing-education or career-technical certificate programs at Iowa community colleges.

scholarships.name: Kentucky Educational Excellence Scholarship (KEES)
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to $500 per year based on GPA plus ACT/AP bonuses
scholarships.description: Merit award for Kentucky high school students who earn a 2.5 GPA or higher, funded by Kentucky Lottery proceeds. Students earn a base amount for each year of high school GPA plus bonus awards for ACT or SAT scores and qualifying AP, IB, or Cambridge exam scores. Funds carry forward automatically to eligible Kentucky colleges and technical schools.

scholarships.name: College Access Program (CAP) Grant
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to $5,300 at four-year schools, up to $2,500 at two-year schools (2026-2027)
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for financially disadvantaged Kentucky undergraduates at eligible in-state institutions. Awarded to students with demonstrated financial need as shown on the FAFSA. Funds are limited and awarded on a first-come basis, so filing the FAFSA early is important.

scholarships.name: Kentucky Tuition Grant (KTG)
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for Kentucky residents attending eligible private nonprofit colleges in the state. Award is based on financial need from the FAFSA and is limited to full-time undergraduate enrollment. Funds are awarded until exhausted, so early FAFSA filing is advised.

scholarships.name: Work Ready Kentucky Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to KCTCS in-state tuition and fees
scholarships.description: Last-dollar scholarship covering tuition for students pursuing an industry-recognized certificate, diploma, or Associate of Applied Science degree in one of Kentucky's high-demand sectors. Eligibility ends after 60 credit hours or completion of a first associate degree. Award pays remaining tuition after other gift aid is applied.

scholarships.name: Dual Credit Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Tuition up to $99 per credit hour (2026-2027)
scholarships.description: Pays tuition for Kentucky high school and homeschool juniors and seniors taking approved dual credit college courses. Covers one general education course per year at a capped per credit hour rate. Application deadlines fall in early October for fall and early March for spring.

scholarships.name: Work Ready Dual Credit Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Actual CTE dual credit course tuition
scholarships.description: Helps Kentucky high school students pay for career and technical education dual credit courses. Covers up to two approved CTE courses per school year at eligible institutions. Award equals the actual tuition charged for the qualifying course.

scholarships.name: Early Childhood Development Scholarship
scholarships.description: Assists workers in Kentucky daycares and preschools who are earning credentials or degrees in early childhood education. Requires at least 20 hours weekly employment in a participating facility and a service commitment after completion. Award supports tuition and related costs toward the credential.

scholarships.name: Teacher Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to $3,000 per fall or spring semester
scholarships.description: Financial aid for Kentucky students pursuing initial teacher certification or additional certifications. Recipients agree to teach one semester at a Kentucky public or certified non-public school for each semester of support received. Award may convert to a loan if the teaching commitment is not met.

scholarships.name: Teacher Recruitment Loan Program
scholarships.amountLabel: Forgivable loan up to $5,000 per semester
scholarships.description: Forgivable loan for Kentucky students admitted to approved teacher education programs. Provides up to $5,000 per semester for students admitted to a college of education and up to $2,500 per semester for students who have declared the major. The loan is forgiven through teaching service in Kentucky public schools.

scholarships.name: Kentucky Optometry Scholarship
scholarships.description: Supports Kentucky residents pursuing a doctor of optometry degree at eligible institutions. Award helps offset the cost of optometry education for qualifying students. Recipients must be Kentucky residents enrolled in an approved optometry program.

scholarships.name: Kentucky Osteopathic Medicine Scholarship
scholarships.description: Assists students at the Kentucky College of Osteopathic Medicine by covering the difference between average in-state Kentucky medical school tuition and KCOM tuition. Recipients agree to practice one year in Kentucky for each scholarship year received.

scholarships.name: Veterinary Contract Spaces Program
scholarships.amountLabel: In-state tuition rate at partner veterinary schools
scholarships.description: Lets Kentucky residents study veterinary medicine at Southern Regional Education Board partner schools at reduced tuition. The program covers the difference between out-of-state and in-state tuition. A limited number of contract spaces are awarded annually for up to eight semesters.

scholarships.name: Kentucky Governor's Scholars Program
scholarships.amountLabel: $5,000 to $10,000 college scholarships via participating schools
scholarships.description: A five-week summer residential program for outstanding Kentucky rising high school seniors, held on Centre College, Morehead State, and Murray State campuses. Students are nominated by their high schools and compete statewide. Completers become eligible for scholarships from many Kentucky colleges, with participating schools offering renewable awards.

scholarships.name: Rogers Scholars
scholarships.amountLabel: College scholarship opportunities from partner colleges
scholarships.description: A week-long leadership and entrepreneurship program for rising high school juniors in the 45-county service region of Southern and Eastern Kentucky. Students apply during their sophomore year and, if selected, attend a tuition-free summer session. Rogers Scholars become eligible for exclusive scholarship offers from partner colleges and universities.

scholarships.name: University of Kentucky Provost Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: $2,500 or $5,000 per year (tiered by GPA and test scores)
scholarships.description: An automatic merit award for admitted University of Kentucky freshmen, including Kentucky residents. Students with a 3.30 GPA and 26 ACT or 1230 SAT earn $2,500 per year, and those with a 3.30 GPA and 28 ACT or 1300 SAT earn $5,000 per year, with test-optional GPA paths available. Renewal requires full-time enrollment and a 3.0 cumulative GPA.

scholarships.name: University of Kentucky Presidential Scholarship
scholarships.description: A competitive award for high-achieving admitted University of Kentucky freshmen covering full in-state tuition. Traditional eligibility is a 3.50 GPA with a 31 ACT or 1390 SAT, with a 4.00 GPA test-optional path. Applicants must complete the competitive scholarship section of the admission application.

scholarships.name: University of Kentucky Otis A. Singletary Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Full in-state tuition plus $10,000 per year housing stipend
scholarships.description: The top competitive merit award for admitted University of Kentucky freshmen, covering full in-state tuition plus a $10,000 per year housing stipend for the first two years on campus. Traditional eligibility is a 3.80 GPA with a 33 ACT or 1450 SAT, with a 4.00 GPA test-optional path. Recipients must maintain a 3.40 cumulative GPA.

scholarships.name: University of Louisville Trustees' Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Amount varies by GPA and test scores
scholarships.description: A merit scholarship for first-time freshmen entering the University of Louisville who reside in Kentucky and eligible Southern Indiana counties. Awards are based on a combination of GPA and test scores. Students are considered by completing the admission application and required materials by the December scholarship deadline.

scholarships.name: University of Louisville Cardinal Commitment Grant
scholarships.description: A need-based grant for Kentucky resident first-time freshmen at the University of Louisville. Eligible students are identified and awarded automatically after federal and state need-based grants, KEES, and institutional aid are considered, with awards ranging up to full tuition coverage. The priority deadline is in mid-February.

scholarships.name: Berea College Tuition Promise Scholarship
scholarships.description: Berea College has charged no tuition since 1892 and provides every admitted student the equivalent of a four-year full-tuition scholarship. Admission favors students with strong academic potential and financial need, with preference for qualified students from the southern Appalachian region, including Kentucky. Financial need is verified through the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Kentucky Farm Bureau Education Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: A statewide scholarship program for Kentucky high school seniors who are the children of Kentucky Farm Bureau members. Awards are made in more than 50 categories, and some awards are also open to nontraditional students. Funds may be applied to tuition, housing, books, or other educational expenses.

scholarships.name: Blue Grass Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.amountLabel: $1,000 to $10,000 per year depending on fund
scholarships.description: The Blue Grass Community Foundation manages more than 50 scholarships serving Central and Appalachian Kentucky, most limited to Kentucky residents. A single application considers students for many funds, most for graduating high school seniors with some for current undergraduate and graduate students. Applications open each December.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Louisville General Scholarships
scholarships.description: The Community Foundation of Louisville awards millions in competitive scholarships each year to students across Kentucky and Southern Indiana. Completing one general application considers students for the more than 90 scholarships they may qualify for. Most awards support Kentucky students, and the application period opens in December.

scholarships.name: Central Kentucky Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: The Central Kentucky Community Foundation administers many scholarships through its Scholarship Central platform for students in its service area. For the coming academic year, students may apply starting January 1 with a March 1 deadline. Applications generally require an official transcript, test scores, and financial information.

scholarships.name: Louisville Branch NAACP Scholarship Awards Program
scholarships.description: Scholarships for graduating high school seniors and undergraduate students who are legal residents of Metro Louisville. High school seniors and undergraduates must hold a 2.5 GPA or higher, and graduate applicants must hold a 3.0 or higher. Applicants must be U.S. citizens enrolled or accepted at an accredited institution.

scholarships.name: Louisville Urban League Scholarship
scholarships.description: A scholarship for Black graduating Jefferson County Public Schools seniors administered by the Louisville Urban League. Applicants must articulate an understanding of and commitment to equity and social justice in their future academic and professional pursuits. Awards are a minimum of $1,000.

scholarships.name: KyCPA Educational Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Educational Foundation of the Kentucky Society of CPAs
scholarships.description: Awards for accounting students at Kentucky colleges, or Kentucky residents attending bordering states, who plan to become CPAs. Applicants need an overall GPA of at least 2.75, completed Intermediate Accounting, free KyCPA student membership, and intent to work in Kentucky after graduation. Applications are accepted from November through mid-February.

scholarships.name: Bonita Compton Scholarship Fund
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to $4,500 (up to two awards annually)
scholarships.description: Supports Floyd County, Kentucky high school graduates pursuing post-secondary education. Applicants must hold a 2.5 GPA or higher. Up to two scholarships are awarded each year through the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky.

scholarships.name: Charles E. Cox Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Jackson County, Kentucky residents pursuing careers in health, social work, mental health, forestry, or sustainable agriculture. Applicants must hold a 3.0 GPA or higher. Administered by the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky.

scholarships.name: Danny and Margaret Maggard Community Service Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Hazard High School graduates with a 3.0 GPA or higher and an interest in community service. Awarded through the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky to support students continuing their education.

scholarships.name: Dean Jones Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Shelby Valley High School seniors in Pike County, Kentucky pursuing careers in community service. Administered by the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky to support students entering service-oriented fields.

scholarships.name: East Kentucky Health Occupation Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Pike County or Betsy Layne High School graduates in Kentucky pursuing healthcare careers. Applicants must hold a 2.5 GPA or higher. Administered by the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky.

scholarships.name: Edith Campbell Educational Endowment
scholarships.description: For Hazard, Perry Central, or Buckhorn High School seniors in Kentucky with a 2.0 GPA or higher. The award is distributed over the duration of the student's program through the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky.

scholarships.name: Reynolds Family Education Award
scholarships.description: For Letcher County or Jenkins Independent School District graduates in Kentucky with a 2.5 unweighted GPA or higher. The award provides $2,000 per year and is renewable for up to four years through the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky.

scholarships.name: Midway University Scholarship (Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky)
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to $10,000 per year (renewable up to 4 years)
scholarships.description: For female Johnson County, Kentucky high school graduates who are single-parent or orphaned students attending Midway University. Applicants must hold a 3.0 GPA or higher and a minimum ACT of 21. The award is renewable for up to four years.

scholarships.name: Mountain Mothers Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: $1,000 for trade school or $2,000 for college
scholarships.description: For female seniors at Shelby Valley or Pikeville High School in Kentucky with a 2.0 GPA or higher. The award is $1,000 for trade school or $2,000 for a college or university, administered by the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky.

scholarships.name: Next Step Scholarship
scholarships.description: For East Ridge High School seniors in Pike County, Kentucky with a 2.5 GPA or higher and a teacher recommendation. Administered by the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky to support students continuing their education.

scholarships.name: Woodrow and Evelyn Johnson Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Shelby Valley High School graduates in Kentucky with a 3.0 GPA or higher who file the FAFSA and plan to attend a Kentucky college or university. Administered by the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky.

scholarships.name: Blackcats Alumni Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For Prestonsburg High School seniors in Kentucky entering a four-year institution, allied health, or skilled trades program. Awards of $1,500 are made in each category through the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky.

scholarships.name: Bertee and Rhetta Faye Adkins Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Betsy Layne High School graduates in Floyd County, Kentucky with a 2.6 GPA or higher who have taken AP courses. Administered by the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky. The award also considers Oliver Springs High School in Tennessee.

scholarships.name: Cartis and Merkie Carpenter Scholarship
scholarships.description: For graduates of North Laurel, South Laurel, Clay County High School, or Oneida Baptist Institute in Kentucky who file the FAFSA. Administered by the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky to support students with financial need.

scholarships.name: Sharon Davis-Angell Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: For graduating seniors from Harlan County, Kentucky and Bledsoe, Kentucky to support students pursuing their educational goals. Administered as a renewable program through the Foundation for Appalachian Kentucky.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma's Promise (OHLAP)
scholarships.organization: Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education
scholarships.description: Early commitment program that covers college tuition at Oklahoma public colleges for students who enroll in 8th through 11th grade, meet family income limits, and complete required coursework. Family income cannot exceed 60000 at application. Students must maintain the required GPA and course requirements.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma Tuition Aid Grant (OTAG)
scholarships.organization: Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education
scholarships.description: Need based grant for Oklahoma residents who are Pell eligible and enrolled at least half time in an undergraduate program at an eligible Oklahoma institution. Awards reach up to 1500 at community colleges, 2000 at regional universities, and 3000 at research universities. Requires the FAFSA. Funds are limited so early filing matters.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma Tuition Equalization Grant (OTEG)
scholarships.organization: Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education
scholarships.description: Need based grant for Oklahoma residents enrolled full time as undergraduates at eligible private or independent Oklahoma colleges. Family income must be 50000 or less with sufficient unmet financial need. Requires the FAFSA each year with Oklahoma listed as state of residence.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma Rising Scholars Award (Academic Scholars Program)
scholarships.organization: Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship for high achieving students who are National Merit Scholars or Finalists, U.S. Presidential Scholars, or who score at or above the 99.5 percentile on the ACT or SAT. Institutions may also nominate qualifying students. Awards range from 4000 to 6000 per year for up to eight semesters and help cover tuition, room, board, and books.

scholarships.name: Inspired to Teach Scholarship and Incentive Program
scholarships.organization: Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education / Oklahoma Teacher Connection
scholarships.description: Program for students preparing to become teachers in Oklahoma. Participants can earn up to 25500 total across their educator preparation program and first years of teaching. Recipients must agree to teach in an Oklahoma public prekindergarten through 12th grade school for at least five consecutive years after graduation and licensure.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma National Guard Educational Assistance
scholarships.organization: Oklahoma National Guard / Oklahoma State Regents
scholarships.description: Tuition waiver covering tuition and mandatory academic service fees for active Oklahoma National Guard members at all Oklahoma public colleges and universities. Members may enroll in up to 18 credit hours per semester up to 120 hours for an undergraduate degree. Requires at least one year remaining on the enlistment contract and a service commitment after the last funded semester.

scholarships.name: OCCF New Opportunities Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for a first generation college student applied for during the junior year of high school in central Oklahoma. Supports students who will be the first in their families to graduate from college. Applications run through the OCCF student portal.

scholarships.name: OCCF Community Foundation Scholars
scholarships.description: Scholarship for graduating seniors from participating high schools in the Central Oklahoma Guidance Counselor Network. Part of the largest independent scholarship provider in Oklahoma, which awards more than 5 million to over 1000 students statewide each year. One application opens access to many funds.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma City Community Foundation Scholarships (General)
scholarships.description: More than 200 scholarship opportunities through a single application for Oklahoma students. Awards range from 2000 to 20000 and many are renewable. The application opens in the fall with rolling program deadlines through February. Students apply at the OCCF AcademicWorks portal.

scholarships.name: Tulsa Community Foundation My Dream / Mi Sueno Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for first time first generation students who enroll at Tulsa Community College directly after graduating from a Tulsa or Rogers County high school with at least a 2.0 GPA. Provides up to 2000 per semester for up to three years or 60 credit hours while enrolled in at least nine hours.

scholarships.name: Tulsa Community Foundation Scholarships (General)
scholarships.description: The foundation manages more than forty scholarship funds serving students locally and nationwide, awarding roughly 20 million each year. Most application windows open in mid February and close by the end of March. Each fund sets its own eligibility rules and priorities.

scholarships.name: Central States Manufacturing Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Scholarship fund administered by the Tulsa Community Foundation supporting students pursuing higher education. The application window opens in mid February with a submission deadline at the end of March. Terms are set by the donor group.

scholarships.name: Communities Foundation of Oklahoma Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 100 scholarship opportunities for Oklahoma students pursuing higher or vocational education. A single Universal Application lets students apply for multiple scholarships at once. Individual program deadlines vary and applications submit through the foundation portal.

scholarships.name: Cherokee Nation Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Cherokee Nation citizens pursuing higher education. The foundation awarded more than 500000 in a recent year, its largest total ever, and students may receive up to two foundation scholarships per academic year. Applications open through the foundation website.

scholarships.name: Cherokee Nation Undergraduate Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Scholarship program from the Cherokee Nation College Resource Center for enrolled Cherokee Nation citizens pursuing undergraduate degrees. Applications are submitted through the Gadugi portal. The program supports tuition and college costs and requires enrollment verification each term.

scholarships.name: Chickasaw Nation Higher Education Grant
scholarships.description: Grants and scholarships for enrolled Chickasaw Nation citizens seeking certification, associate, bachelor, or graduate degrees. Fall applications run July 1 to September 15 and spring applications run December 1 to February 15. Students may be full or part time and must hold Chickasaw citizenship.

scholarships.name: Choctaw Nation Higher Education Program
scholarships.description: Scholarship for members of the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma pursuing a degree at an accredited institution while registered for at least three credit hours. Application periods are August 1 to October 1 for fall, January 2 to March 1 for spring, and May 1 to June 15 for summer. A minimum 2.0 GPA is required for funding.

scholarships.name: Muscogee (Creek) Nation Higher Education Scholarship
scholarships.description: Higher education scholarship for citizens of the Muscogee Creek Nation. Fall applications open in the spring and close in mid June, with all required materials due in full by the deadline. Administered by the Muscogee Nation Department of Education and Training.

scholarships.name: Muscogee Nation Aristocrat (Cokv Hecv) Honors Scholarship
scholarships.description: Honors scholarship of 5000 for Mvskoke scholars who demonstrate leadership, participation, and community service. Applications are due in mid June with a firm submission deadline. Awarded for the academic year to citizens of the Muscogee Creek Nation.

scholarships.name: Osage Nation Higher Education Scholarship
