scholarships.description: Scholarship for Osage students pursuing post secondary education at the associate level or beyond, including bachelor, master, and doctoral programs at accredited schools. Students must submit the Annual Qualifying Application and maintain a minimum 2.0 GPA each term in good standing.

scholarships.name: Citizen Potawatomi Nation College and University Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Citizen Potawatomi Nation Department of Education
scholarships.description: Scholarship providing tuition assistance for enrolled Citizen Potawatomi Nation members pursuing undergraduate or graduate degrees. Full time students may receive up to 2000 per semester and part time students up to 750. The fall window opens July 15 and closes September 15.

scholarships.name: University of Oklahoma Award of Excellence
scholarships.description: Automatic merit scholarship for incoming freshmen with a 31 ACT or 1390 SAT and a 3.5 GPA. Renewable over four years. Students are considered automatically when they apply for admission, and test optional applicants are reviewed holistically.

scholarships.name: University of Oklahoma National Merit Finalist Scholarship (Resident)
scholarships.description: Scholarship package for Oklahoma resident National Merit Finalists who attend the University of Oklahoma. The multi year package supports tuition, fees, and living costs and is among the most generous merit awards offered by the university.

scholarships.name: University of Oklahoma Sooner Heritage Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need based scholarship established to help middle income students whose families may not qualify for federal aid but still need help with college costs. Awards are based on financial need from the FAFSA and give priority to families with more than one child in college. Undergraduates must enroll in at least six hours per semester.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma State University Freshman Academic Scholarships
scholarships.description: Freshmen are automatically considered for academic scholarships when they apply for admission to Oklahoma State University. Selection considers academic performance, test scores, class rank, resume, and essay. The early opportunity deadline is November 1 and all materials are due by February 1 for fall entry.

scholarships.name: OSU Horizon Scholars Program
scholarships.description: New four year scholarship initiative backed by 12 million in private donations from alumni families. Beginning with the fall 2026 freshman class, selected students receive up to 43000 in total support across their degree. Students are considered through the freshman scholarship process.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma Hall of Fame Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Oklahoma high school seniors who commit to attending an Oklahoma college or university. Selection is based on leadership roles, civic and community engagement, academic achievement, and extracurricular involvement. Students must be recommended by an unrelated teacher, administrator, or adult.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma FFA Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Oklahoma FFA members pursuing agriculture education at trade schools, certification programs, or colleges. Sponsored by Oklahoma businesses and organizations such as Oklahoma Farm Bureau. Awards recognize state interscholastic winners and support high school seniors and collegiate members.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma 4-H Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for active Oklahoma 4-H members based on 4-H involvement, leadership, community service, and academic achievement. Administered through Oklahoma State University Extension. Awards support graduating seniors and current college students continuing their education.

scholarships.name: University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma Freshman Scholarships
scholarships.organization: University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma
scholarships.description: Academic scholarships for first time freshmen at the University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma in Chickasha. Awards are based on GPA and test scores and are renewable with continued academic performance. Students apply through admission to the university.

scholarships.name: University of Central Oklahoma Incoming Freshman Scholarships
scholarships.description: Merit scholarships for incoming freshmen at the University of Central Oklahoma in Edmond. Awards are based on GPA and test scores, with automatic consideration through the admission and scholarship application. Several tiers are renewable across multiple years.

scholarships.name: Oklahoma Baptist University Freshman Scholarships
scholarships.description: Academic merit scholarships for incoming freshmen at Oklahoma Baptist University in Shawnee. Awards are based on GPA and test scores and are renewable. Students are considered automatically when admitted to the university.

scholarships.name: Ford Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarship for graduating Oregon high school seniors pursuing a first bachelor's degree at an in-state college full time. Award is calculated from financial need and cost of attendance. No minimum GPA to apply.

scholarships.name: Ford Transfer Program
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarship for Oregon community college students transferring as juniors to a four-year in-state institution to earn a first bachelor's degree. Award reflects financial need and cost of attendance.

scholarships.name: Ford Opportunity Program
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarship for Oregon parents (especially single parents) and adults over 25 who are not parenting, pursuing a first bachelor's degree at an in-state college. Award reflects financial need.

scholarships.name: Ford Sons and Daughters Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for eligible dependents of Roseburg Forest Products employees pursuing higher education. Administered through the Ford Family Foundation scholarship programs.

scholarships.name: OSAC Scholarship Application
scholarships.organization: Oregon Office of Student Access and Completion
scholarships.description: A single online application that matches Oregon students to more than 600 scholarships totaling over $10 million each year. Opens November 1 with an early-bird deadline in mid-February and a final deadline of March 1.

scholarships.name: Oregon Opportunity Grant
scholarships.organization: Oregon Office of Student Access and Completion
scholarships.description: Oregon's largest state-funded need-based grant, serving more than 40,000 low-income resident students each year toward a first associate or bachelor's degree. Award depends on financial need and institution type. Requires FAFSA or ORSAA.

scholarships.name: Oregon Promise Grant
scholarships.organization: Oregon Office of Student Access and Completion
scholarships.description: Last-dollar grant that covers most community college tuition for recent Oregon high school or GED graduates after Pell and the Oregon Opportunity Grant are applied. Most students must apply during their senior year.

scholarships.name: Oregon Tribal Student Grant
scholarships.organization: Oregon Office of Student Access and Completion
scholarships.description: Grant for enrolled members of one of Oregon's nine federally recognized tribes attending an Oregon college at least half time. Covers average cost of attendance after other federal and state aid. Priority deadline September 30.

scholarships.name: Oregon Teacher Scholars Program Grant
scholarships.organization: Oregon Office of Student Access and Completion
scholarships.description: Grant for racially, ethnically, and linguistically diverse candidates pursuing teacher licensure, school counseling, social work, or psychology at an approved Oregon educator preparation program. Up to two academic years of funding on a rolling deadline.

scholarships.name: Apex Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit award for admitted Oregon resident freshmen, paid $2,000 per year for four years. Applied automatically based on the admission application. Combinable with several other UO scholarships.

scholarships.name: Summit Scholarship
scholarships.description: Top merit award for admitted Oregon resident freshmen, paid $5,000 per year for four years. Awarded from the admission application to Oregon's strongest scholars. Cannot be combined with the Apex Scholarship.

scholarships.name: PathwayOregon
scholarships.description: Guarantee of full tuition and fees plus advising for academically qualified, Pell-eligible Oregonians who graduate from an Oregon high school. Funded through a mix of federal, state, and UO aid. Requires admission by January 15 and annual FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Finley Academic Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit award for new Oregon resident freshmen at OSU Corvallis or Bend, typically with a 3.50 unweighted GPA or higher. Awarded from the admission application and renewable for up to four years total.

scholarships.name: Oregon Latino Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for students of Hispanic ancestry residing in Oregon or Clark County, Washington who attended high school there, with a 3.0 GPA and enrollment at a community college, university, or graduate program. First-generation and DACA students encouraged.

scholarships.name: Southern Oregon Latino Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: Scholarship supporting Latino students from southern Oregon pursuing higher education, awarded on academics, community involvement, and need. Administered by the Redwood Foundation for Education.

scholarships.name: Black United Fund of Oregon Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for high school seniors and current college students of African-American, African Diaspora, Black, or Afro descent attending Oregon colleges. Multiple named awards are offered through one application.

scholarships.name: Abe and Sol Blackman Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for economically disadvantaged Black male graduates of Rosemary Anderson High School in Portland pursuing postsecondary education. Administered by the Oregon Community Foundation.

scholarships.name: Salem-Keizer NAACP High School Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Black high school students in the Salem-Keizer area attending a four-year college or university, with a minimum 2.5 GPA. Awarded by the local NAACP branch.

scholarships.name: Pride Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: One application covering 60+ scholarships for current and future LGBTQ+ leaders from Oregon (or the greater Northwest) facing significant barriers, pursuing any postsecondary path. Application opens in October and closes in early January.

scholarships.name: Oregon Farm Bureau Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Statewide scholarship for Oregon high school graduates majoring in agriculture or forestry, or children/grandchildren of voting Farm Bureau members, with a 3.0 GPA and full-time enrollment. Not based on financial need; renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Oregon Nurseries Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: About 20 awards for students preparing for a career in ornamental horticulture and related fields, judged on career interest, scholastic aptitude, and financial need. Applications open January 1 and close in mid-April.

scholarships.name: Renaissance Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarship for first-generation Oregon high school seniors with significant financial need who will be the first in their family to earn a bachelor's degree. Renewable up to four years with a 3.0 GPA and 12+ credits per term.

scholarships.name: Oregon Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: One of the largest scholarship programs of its kind in the country, awarding thousands of scholarships each year across many majors and backgrounds. Apply through OSAC for 500+ funds or the MyOCF portal for OCF-only awards. Deadline March 2.

scholarships.name: Oregon Logging Conference Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Ten to fourteen awards each year for students studying forestry-related fields at two-year or four-year schools. Funds may be used for tuition and books. Applications open in December and close April 1.

scholarships.name: Oregon State Elks Association Vocational Scholarship
scholarships.description: Five awards of $2,000 each for Oregon residents seeking a professional certification or associate degree in a vocational or technical trade field. No age restriction; open to any Oregon resident.

scholarships.name: Umatilla-Morrow County Farm Bureau Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for high school seniors in Umatilla and Morrow counties, with priority to applicants who have an agricultural background, FFA involvement, or an intended agriculture-related major.

scholarships.name: Benton County Farm Bureau Scholarship
scholarships.description: Three scholarships for Benton County residents studying agriculture or forestry at a college or university. Awarded by the county Farm Bureau.

scholarships.name: Klamath-Lake County Farm Bureau Scholarship
scholarships.description: Three $1,000 scholarships for graduating high school seniors from Klamath or Lake County. Awarded by the county Farm Bureau.

scholarships.name: Malheur County Farm Bureau Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for students from Farm Bureau member families in Malheur County pursuing an agriculture-related field.

scholarships.name: Coos-Curry County Farm Bureau Scholarship
scholarships.description: Two $2,000 scholarships for high school seniors or current college students from Coos or Curry County. Awarded by the county Farm Bureau.

scholarships.name: Douglas County Farm Bureau Scholarship
scholarships.description: Up to five $1,000 scholarships for Douglas County high school seniors or recent graduates with an interest in agriculture or forestry.

scholarships.name: Yamhill County Farm Bureau Scholarship
scholarships.description: Three scholarships for college sophomores and above majoring in agriculture, with a minimum 2.5 GPA. Awarded by the county Farm Bureau.

scholarships.name: Utah Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: Statewide merit scholarship for Utah high school graduates who complete advanced AP, IB, or concurrent enrollment courses in math, science, and language arts. Requires a 3.3 cumulative GPA, FAFSA completion, and enrollment at an eligible Utah institution.

scholarships.name: Utah Promise Grant
scholarships.description: Need-based grant that expands access to higher education for Utah residents. Covers remaining costs after other aid at Utah public colleges, technical colleges, and eligible private nonprofit institutions. Requires FAFSA and demonstrated financial need.

scholarships.name: First Credential Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Utah System of Higher Education / Utah State Board of Education
scholarships.description: One-time award for Utah high school seniors who complete a college-preparation pathway: five general education concurrent enrollment courses, six or more CTE courses or 300 hours at a Utah technical college, or 300 hours toward an approved youth apprenticeship. Requires the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: T.H. Bell Education Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Tuition, fees, and books (up to 4 years)
scholarships.description: Supports students pursuing an approved teacher education or speech language pathology program who commit to working in a Utah public school after graduation. Priority is given to first-generation students and those planning to teach in high-need areas. Requires the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Karen Mayne Public Safety Officer Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Utah high school graduates entering public safety careers. Recipients enroll in a state-certified academy basic training course, pursue a criminal justice degree, and commit to five years as a certified peace officer in Utah. Requires the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Veterans Tuition Gap Program
scholarships.description: Helps Utah veterans complete their final year of a bachelor's degree after federal VA education benefits are exhausted. Awarded through the enrolling institution based on need and available funding.

scholarships.name: Adult Learner Grant
scholarships.description: Provides financial assistance to adult learners (age 26 and older) enrolled in eligible online programs aligned with high-demand industry fields at Utah institutions.

scholarships.name: Technical Education Scholarship
scholarships.description: Assists Utah students pursuing technical certificates in high-demand industries at Utah technical colleges and degree-granting institutions.

scholarships.name: Talent Development Award Program
scholarships.description: Recruits and trains Utah residents for high-demand, high-wage jobs by funding education in targeted career pathways at eligible Utah institutions.

scholarships.name: Public Safety Officer Career Advancement Grant (PSOCAG)
scholarships.amountLabel: 50% of tuition and fees, up to $5,000/year
scholarships.description: For certified Utah peace officers pursuing a criminal justice-related degree. Covers half of tuition and fees up to $5,000 per year for as many as eight years at eligible Utah institutions.

scholarships.name: First Responder Mental Health Services Grant
scholarships.description: Funds Utah first responders pursuing degrees or certificates in mental health therapy, supporting the pipeline of behavioral health providers for first responder communities.

scholarships.name: NASA Space Grant Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Utah System of Higher Education / Utah NASA Space Grant Consortium
scholarships.description: Supports Utah students in aerospace-related programs who intend to pursue aerospace careers, administered through Utah's higher education system and the Utah NASA Space Grant Consortium.

scholarships.name: Utah National Guard State Tuition Assistance (STA)
scholarships.description: Tuition assistance for Utah National Guard members attending a Utah public college or university full time. Members must be MOS/AFSC qualified, lack a four-year degree, and commit to two additional years of Guard service. Applied for each semester.

scholarships.name: For Utah Scholarship
scholarships.description: Covers four years of tuition and fees for Pell-eligible Utah residents at the University of Utah. Requires the University of Utah application by December 1 and the FAFSA by February 1, with continued Pell eligibility and a 3.0 GPA to renew.

scholarships.name: Utah Promise Scholarship
scholarships.description: Beginning Fall 2026, guarantees full tuition and mandatory fees for first-time, first-year Utah residents whose family household income and assets are each under $100,000. Requires a 3.5 unweighted GPA, admission by December 1, and the FAFSA by February 1.

scholarships.name: Larry H. and Gail Miller Enrichment Scholarship
scholarships.organization: University of Utah / Larry H. and Gail Miller Family Foundation
scholarships.amountLabel: Full tuition, fees, room, board, and books
scholarships.description: Full-support scholarship for University of Utah students whose racial or ethnic background is underrepresented in Utah higher education or who are first-generation college students. Covers tuition, fees, on-campus room and board, and a textbook allowance.

scholarships.name: Dream Weber Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Full tuition and general student fees
scholarships.description: Provides free tuition and general fees for Utah-resident undergraduates with household income of $50,000 or less who qualify for a Pell Grant. Requires enrollment in 12 to 18 credits and a 2.0 GPA to maintain, for up to eight semesters.

scholarships.name: Utah-Resident Freshman Scholarship
scholarships.description: Automatic merit scholarship for first-time Utah-resident freshmen at Utah Tech University. Tiers range from the Merit award ($1,000/year, 3.0 GPA) up to the Presidential award (full tuition). Requires complete admission with transcripts and test scores by March 1.

scholarships.name: Thor's Pledge Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Covers tuition gap after other aid
scholarships.description: For Pell-eligible Utah-resident students at Southern Utah University, filling the gap between other grants and scholarships and the cost of tuition. Requires the FAFSA and admission to SUU.

scholarships.name: America First Charitable Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awards ten $5,000 scholarships to America First Credit Union members who are graduating Utah high school seniors or current college students with a 3.0 GPA and a record of community service. Requires an essay, transcript, and two letters of recommendation.

scholarships.name: Geneva Rock Scholarship Essay Contest
scholarships.description: Awards $2,000 twice a year to students enrolled or soon enrolling at an accredited Utah university, college, trade, or vocational school pursuing a construction-related career such as construction management, civil engineering, welding, diesel tech, or heavy equipment operation. Requires essay responses and a work photo.

scholarships.name: Daniels Scholarship Program
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to full cost of attendance
scholarships.description: Four-year scholarship for graduating seniors in Utah, Colorado, New Mexico, and Wyoming with financial need (family AGI $100,000 or less), a 3.0 GPA, and qualifying ACT or SAT scores. Covers costs beyond other aid and includes a laptop and support services.

scholarships.name: Utah Somos Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Supports Latino and Hispanic high school seniors and undergraduates who live and study in Utah, demonstrate financial need, and show community involvement and leadership. Applies to two- or four-year colleges, certificate, or trade programs in Utah.

scholarships.name: Hogan & Associates Construction Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awards five $1,000 scholarships to Utah high school seniors or recent GED/HISET graduates pursuing a trade, associate degree, or Construction Management degree in a construction-related field such as electrical, HVAC, or plumbing.

scholarships.name: Career and Technical Education Scholarships and Tuition Awards
scholarships.description: Sponsored by the Utah State Board of Education for Utah public high school seniors enrolled in Career and Technical Education programs. Awards range from $1,000 to full tuition and are administered through participating Utah technical colleges and universities.

scholarships.name: Italian American Civic League Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Italian American Civic League of Utah
scholarships.description: Awarded to Utah high school seniors of Italian ancestry planning to attend college. Awards range from $1,000 to $4,000 based on the applicant pool and available funding.

scholarships.name: Call to Action Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarship for Utah high school seniors with demonstrated financial need who plan to attend college. Provides significant annual support toward tuition and college costs.

scholarships.name: Greenhouse Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Whole-person scholarship and mentoring program for high-performing Utah high school seniors with financial need and a 3.5 or higher GPA who are passionate about community service. Combines financial support with leadership development.

scholarships.name: Sterling Scholar Awards of Utah
scholarships.organization: Deseret News / KSL Sterling Scholar Program
scholarships.description: Recognizes outstanding Utah high school seniors across fourteen academic categories, from mathematics to world languages. Regional and state finalists receive cash awards and college scholarships; the program awards tens of thousands of dollars annually.

scholarships.name: University of Utah Latin American Studies Scholarship
scholarships.organization: University of Utah College of Humanities
scholarships.description: Provides financial assistance to promising lower-income University of Utah students who speak a Latin American language at home and are interested in studying the languages, history, cultures, or societies of Latin American countries.

scholarships.name: Larry H. and Gail Miller Foundation & Union Scholarship for Veteran Students
scholarships.organization: University of Utah / Larry H. and Gail Miller Foundation
scholarships.description: Provides four $2,500 scholarships to student veterans at the University of Utah to help them accomplish their academic goals.

scholarships.name: David Arapene Cuch Scholarship
scholarships.organization: University of Utah S.J. Quinney College of Law
scholarships.description: Provides financial support for members of the Ute Indian Tribe who attend law school at the University of Utah, established to honor David Cuch and support Ute students pursuing legal education.

scholarships.name: Associated General Contractors of Utah Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Utah students pursuing construction management, engineering, or skilled-trade careers in the construction industry, offered through the state contractors association.

scholarships.name: President's Scholarship (Resident)
scholarships.description: Automatic merit scholarship for high-achieving Utah-resident freshmen admitted to the University of Utah, awarded based on GPA and test scores. Requires admission by the December 1 priority deadline.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Academic Challenge Scholarship
scholarships.description: Lottery-funded scholarship for Arkansas residents attending in-state two-year or four-year colleges. Traditional and non-traditional students, public, private, homeschool and GED graduates all qualify. Requires FAFSA and enrollment at an eligible Arkansas institution.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Future Grant (ArFuture)
scholarships.description: Covers tuition and fees for certificate and associate degree programs in STEM or state and regional high-demand fields at Arkansas public two-year institutions. Recipients complete FAFSA, meet a mentor each semester, and perform community service. Available first-come, first-served.

scholarships.name: Governor's Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Merit award for academically distinguished Arkansas high school seniors based on GPA and test scores, usable at eligible Arkansas colleges and universities. Renewable for four years with continued academic performance.

scholarships.name: Governor's Distinguished Scholarship
scholarships.description: Most competitive Arkansas state award for top academic achievers, covering up to $10,000 per year for tuition, fees, room and board at eligible Arkansas institutions. Based on ACT/SAT scores plus GPA or National Merit status. Renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Workforce Challenge Scholarship
scholarships.description: Lottery-funded award for students pursuing certificates or credentials in high-demand fields including advanced manufacturing, healthcare, information technology, construction and transportation/logistics at approved Arkansas programs.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Teacher Academy Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Award for students accepted into an Arkansas teacher preparation program who commit to teach in the state after graduation. Preference given to juniors and seniors in eligible education programs.

scholarships.name: ACCESS to Acceleration Scholarship (A2A)
scholarships.description: Supports Arkansas high school students enrolled in concurrent (college-credit) courses, paying $65 per course credit hour up to $2,000 annually. Replaces the former Concurrent Challenge Scholarship and is coordinated through the student's school.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Heroes Scholarship
scholarships.description: Covers tuition, mandatory fees and on-campus housing for spouses and dependents of Arkansas armed forces members, law enforcement officers and other qualifying public safety personnel. Consolidates the former Military Dependents and Law Enforcement Officer's Dependents scholarships.

scholarships.name: Governor's Higher Education Transition Scholarship
scholarships.description: Supports Arkansas students with intellectual and developmental disabilities enrolled in accredited inclusive postsecondary education programs. Provides up to eight semesters of funding.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Transfer Achievement Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Arkansas Division of Higher Education / UA System
scholarships.amountLabel: Matches remaining tuition after other aid
scholarships.description: For Arkansas residents who earn an associate degree at a participating UA System two-year institution and transfer to a University of Arkansas campus. The award matches tuition and is renewable for up to five years with a 2.0 GPA.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Single Parent Scholarship Fund
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to $1,600 per term (scales with credit hours)
scholarships.description: Awards for low-to-moderate income single parents in Arkansas with at least 50% custody of a child under 18 who are enrolled in college, community college or trade school. Funds go directly to the recipient and can cover any expense including childcare, gas and supplies. Awarded fall, spring and summer.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: A single online portal to dozens of donor-established scholarships for Arkansas students attending two- or four-year colleges, vocational or technical schools. A guided quiz matches applicants to funds by county, high school, major or activity. Portal opens February 1 each year.

scholarships.name: Oaklawn Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Arkansas Community Foundation (Hot Springs Area Community Foundation)
scholarships.description: For residents of Garland County, Arkansas pursuing community college, technical or trade programs, or four-year and graduate study. Applicants submit an essay, transcript and proof of county residency. Application window runs January 2 to February 20.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission Conservation Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Arkansas residents attending an in-state accredited college full-time in a conservation-related major such as wildlife biology, fisheries, forestry, environmental science, botany or natural resources. Requires a 2.75 GPA and 40 volunteer hours with the Commission. Up to six awards per class level.

scholarships.name: THEA Foundation Creative Writing Scholarship
scholarships.description: Statewide competition for Arkansas high school seniors submitting fictional short stories, prose or poetry. Ten scholarships awarded, from $10,000 for first place down to $3,000 for places six through ten. Part of Thea's arts-based scholarship program.

scholarships.name: THEA Foundation Visual Arts Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awards ten scholarships each year to Arkansas high school seniors who submit visual art including sculpture, ceramics, and paintings in oil, pastel, watercolor or acrylic. Judged on portfolio submission through the foundation's arts scholarship program.

scholarships.name: THEA Foundation Performing Arts Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship competition for Arkansas high school seniors in performing arts disciplines such as vocal, instrumental, dance and theatre. Part of Thea Foundation's suite of arts scholarships supporting young Arkansas artists.

scholarships.name: El Dorado Promise
scholarships.organization: El Dorado Public Schools / Murphy Oil
scholarships.amountLabel: Tuition and mandatory fees (up to 5 years)
scholarships.description: Covers tuition and mandatory fees for graduates of El Dorado High School who have been continuously enrolled in the El Dorado School District since at least ninth grade. Usable at any accredited college; recipients maintain a 2.0 GPA and full-time enrollment.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Rice Reps Scholarship
scholarships.description: Leadership and social media program for Arkansas high school juniors and rising seniors from any county who advocate for Arkansas agriculture. Participants earn scholarship money through social media contests, video and recipe submissions and leadership awards. No agricultural background required.

scholarships.name: Carl Tapp Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Arkansas high school seniors enrolling in a medium and heavy-duty truck technician program (minimum two semesters) at an Arkansas institution. Supports growth in the state's diesel technician workforce.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Farm Bureau Scholarship Foundation
scholarships.description: For children and grandchildren of Arkansas Farm Bureau members pursuing agriculture studies at an accredited Arkansas university. The foundation distributes over $160,000 in scholarships annually alongside county-level Farm Bureau awards.

scholarships.name: Romeo E. Short Scholarship Foundation
scholarships.description: For students enrolled in the Dale Bumpers College of Agriculture, Food and Life Sciences at the University of Arkansas. Administered through the Bumpers College scholarship application in partnership with Arkansas Farm Bureau.

scholarships.name: Hispanic Women's Organization of Arkansas Scholarship
scholarships.description: Supports Latino students in Arkansas, many of them first-generation college students, attending two- or four-year colleges or community college. HWOA has awarded more than 550 scholarships to date.

scholarships.name: University of Arkansas Chancellor's Scholarship
scholarships.description: Top merit award for incoming Arkansas resident freshmen at the University of Arkansas, selected from the applicant pool. Renewable for four years with a 3.00 GPA and 30 credit hours per year. Requires the admission and scholarship application.

scholarships.name: University of Arkansas Silas Hunt Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to incoming University of Arkansas freshmen demonstrating academic leadership, with consideration of first-generation status, financial need and Arkansas geographic representation. Named for the first African American student admitted to the university.

scholarships.name: University of Arkansas Advance Arkansas Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need-based award for incoming Arkansas resident freshmen at the University of Arkansas who complete the FAFSA, with preference given to first-generation college students. Renewable across the undergraduate years.

scholarships.name: University of Arkansas Razorback Bridge Scholarship
scholarships.description: For incoming Arkansas resident freshmen at the University of Arkansas, considering first-generation status, financial need and geographic representation across the state. Renewable with continued eligibility.

scholarships.name: University of Arkansas Chancellor's Community Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit award for incoming Arkansas freshmen at the University of Arkansas who demonstrate a strong commitment to community service. Selected from top candidates in the applicant pool and renewable.

scholarships.name: Arkansas State University Trailblazer Scholarship
scholarships.description: For high-achieving incoming freshmen at Arkansas State University (Jonesboro), starting Fall 2026. Provides $10,000 per year renewable for up to four years. Recipients maintain a 3.5 GPA and enroll in at least 15 credit hours each fall and spring.

scholarships.name: Arkansas State University Promise Plus Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Arkansas resident freshmen at Arkansas State University with household income under $70,000, a 3.0 high school GPA and a qualifying ACT (19+) or SAT score. Can cover up to full tuition when combined with other aid.

scholarships.name: Don Tyson Endowed Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Springdale Public Schools Education Foundation / Tyson Foods
scholarships.description: For graduates of an accredited public high school in Springdale, Arkansas pursuing postsecondary study at the University of Arkansas Dale Bumpers College of Agriculture, Food and Life Sciences.

scholarships.name: Arkansas Community Colleges Academic All-Star Scholarship
scholarships.description: Recognizes Arkansas two-year college students for scholarship, leadership, social awareness and community service. Recipients are nominated by their community college and transfer to an Arkansas four-year university, where the award helps cover tuition and fees.

scholarships.name: Kansas State Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for academically distinguished Kansas high school graduates who complete the Kansas Scholars Curriculum, take the ACT by December of senior year, are designated Kansas State Scholars, and demonstrate financial need.

scholarships.name: Kansas Comprehensive Grant
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for Kansas residents enrolled full-time at the six state universities, Washburn, or eligible private Kansas colleges. About one in three eligible students is funded; FAFSA required.

scholarships.name: Kansas Ethnic Minority Scholarship
scholarships.description: Need-based award for academically competitive Kansas residents who are African American, American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian or Pacific Islander, or Hispanic, with an ACT of 21, SAT above 1060, or a 3.0 GPA. FAFSA required.

scholarships.name: Kansas Promise Act Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Full tuition, fees, books and supplies
scholarships.description: Last-dollar scholarship covering tuition, fees, books and materials for Kansas residents in high-demand two-year programs at eligible community and technical colleges. Household income caps apply; recipients agree to live and work in Kansas two years after completion.

scholarships.name: Kansas Teacher Service Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit award for students pursuing teaching in hard-to-fill disciplines or underserved Kansas areas. Recipients teach one year in Kansas for each year of support, up to ten semesters.

scholarships.name: Kansas Nursing Service Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for students training as LPNs or RNs who commit to practice in Kansas one year for each year of support received, with a sponsor employer.

scholarships.name: Kansas Education Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit and need-based award for first-generation college students and dependents of Kansas teachers or paraprofessionals attending eligible Kansas institutions.

scholarships.name: Kansas Military Service Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Tuition and fees at public institutions
scholarships.description: Covers tuition and fees at Kansas public institutions for residents who served in military operations receiving hostile-fire pay for 90+ days after September 11, 2001, with an honorable discharge.

scholarships.name: Kansas National Guard Educational Assistance
scholarships.amountLabel: Tuition and fees at Kansas public institutions
scholarships.description: Covers tuition and fees for enlisted Kansas Air and Army National Guard members and their dependents at Kansas public institutions. Full-time enrollment not required.

scholarships.name: Kansas Adult Learner Grant
scholarships.description: Grant for Kansas residents aged 25 and older pursuing bachelor's degrees in high-demand fields including IT, healthcare, nursing, science, engineering, education, and business. Awards are first-come, first-served.

scholarships.name: Foster Child Education Assistance Program
scholarships.description: Tuition and fee assistance at Kansas public institutions for students who experienced foster care in Kansas, supporting their pursuit of a first undergraduate degree or certificate.

scholarships.name: KU Kansas Resident Freshman Merit Scholarships
scholarships.description: Automatic GPA-based awards for incoming Kansas resident freshmen, from the Jayhawk award (3.25 GPA, $4,000) up to the Chancellor award (3.95+ GPA, $20,000). Apply for admission with a transcript by December 1.

scholarships.name: K-State Kansas Resident Academic Merit Scholarships
scholarships.description: Automatic merit awards for Kansas resident incoming freshmen based on GPA and test score, from the 1863 Landmark award ($4,000) up to the University Scholar award ($20,000). The admission application serves as the scholarship application.

scholarships.name: Kansas Hispanic Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Wichita-metro high school seniors of 50% or more Hispanic heritage enrolling full-time at an accredited trade program, community college, or four-year institution. U.S. citizens, DACA, and undocumented students eligible.

scholarships.name: Koch Hispanic Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Renewable award for Wichita-metro high school seniors of 50% or more Hispanic heritage who are U.S. citizens enrolling full-time at a four-year college, with preference for business or engineering majors. Requires a 3.0 GPA for renewal.

scholarships.name: Hispanic Development Fund Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Hispanic Development Fund (Greater Kansas City Community Foundation)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Hispanic/Latino students who graduated from a Greater Kansas City metro high school (Cass, Clay, Jackson, Platte in Missouri; Johnson, Wyandotte in Kansas) and enroll full-time at an accredited college. Reviewed on merit, need, and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Black Community Scholarship Fund
scholarships.organization: Black Community Fund (Greater Kansas City Community Foundation)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for students of African American heritage in the six-county Kansas City metro (including Wyandotte and Johnson counties in Kansas) who are graduating seniors, current college students, or adult learners. Recipients complete 16 hours of community service.

scholarships.name: Greater Kansas City Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Hundreds of scholarship funds administered through a single general application for students in and around the Kansas City area, matching applicants to awards based on their profile. Over $5 million awarded to 2,400+ students in a recent year.

scholarships.name: Wichita Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Multiple scholarship funds for Wichita-area students attending accredited colleges, universities, and technical schools, awarded through a single portal that matches applicants by skills and financial need. Applications open January 1.

scholarships.name: Topeka Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 100 scholarship funds for Topeka-area high school seniors and college students, awarded through one application. Recent recipients shared over $205,000.

scholarships.name: Dane G. Hansen Leaders of Tomorrow Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awards for high school seniors from 26 Northwest Kansas counties attending an accredited four-year Kansas college or university. Renewable for three additional years if committee criteria are met.

scholarships.name: Dane G. Hansen Scholar Scholarship
scholarships.description: Up to 35 awards for qualified high school seniors from 26 Northwest Kansas counties, renewable for three additional years if committee criteria are met.

scholarships.name: Dane G. Hansen Career and Technical Education Scholarship
scholarships.description: Up to 100 awards for high school seniors from 26 Northwest Kansas counties pursuing career and technical education, renewable for one additional year if committee criteria are met.

scholarships.name: Kansas Farm Bureau Foundation for Agriculture Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Kansas Farm Bureau Foundation for Agriculture
scholarships.description: Up to 47 scholarships for students attending Kansas universities and community or technical colleges who show commitment to agriculture, leadership, and community involvement. The student or a parent must hold an active Kansas Farm Bureau membership.

scholarships.name: Kansas Osteopathic Medical Service Scholarship
scholarships.description: Service scholarship for students at accredited osteopathic medical schools who agree to practice in Kansas, encouraging rural practice. Recipients return one year of service for each year of assistance.

scholarships.name: James B. Pearson Fellowship
scholarships.description: Fellowship encouraging study abroad for graduate students from Kansas public universities, particularly those pursuing foreign affairs or international studies.

scholarships.name: Kansas ROTC Service Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for students who commission as a Second Lieutenant and commit to four years of service in the Kansas Army National Guard, available at select Kansas universities and community colleges.

scholarships.name: Kansas Hero's Scholarship
scholarships.description: Tuition and fee waivers for eligible dependents and spouses of deceased or disabled public safety officers, military personnel, and prisoners of war. First-come, first-served with limited funding.

scholarships.name: Kansas Nurse Educator Service Scholarship
scholarships.description: Support for graduate nursing students who commit to teach at a participating Kansas postsecondary institution, teaching one year for each year of assistance after graduation.

scholarships.name: Kansas Distinguished Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Reimburses tuition and fees for recipients of prestigious national scholarships (Fulbright, Rhodes, Marshall, Truman, Madison, Mellon, Chevening, Brasenose) who continue graduate study at a Kansas public university.

scholarships.name: Mississippi Tuition Assistance Grant (MTAG)
scholarships.organization: Mississippi Office of State Financial Aid
scholarships.description: State grant for Mississippi residents attending an approved in state college full time. Pays $500 per year to freshmen and sophomores and $1,000 per year to juniors and seniors. Requires a 2.5 GPA and at least a 15 on the ACT.

scholarships.name: Mississippi Eminent Scholars Grant (MESG)
scholarships.organization: Mississippi Office of State Financial Aid
scholarships.description: Merit grant for high achieving Mississippi residents attending an approved in state college full time. Requires a 3.5 high school GPA and a 29 or higher ACT, a 1350 or higher SAT, or National Merit recognition.

scholarships.name: Higher Education Legislative Plan (HELP) Grant
scholarships.organization: Mississippi Office of State Financial Aid
scholarships.description: Need based grant that pays full tuition for up to four years for Mississippi residents. Requires a 2.5 high school GPA, a minimum 20 ACT, completion of the FAFSA, and family income within state limits.

scholarships.name: Nissan Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Mississippi Office of State Financial Aid
scholarships.amountLabel: Full tuition, fees, and book allowance
scholarships.description: Awards full tuition, fees, and a book allowance to graduating Mississippi high school seniors who show financial need and leadership. Requires a 2.5 GPA and a 20 ACT. Applicants write a short essay on supporting the automotive industry in Mississippi.

scholarships.name: FAITH Scholarship (Fostering Access and Inspiring True Hope)
scholarships.organization: Mississippi Office of State Financial Aid
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to full cost of attendance
scholarships.description: Covers up to the full cost of attendance for Mississippi students who spent time in the state foster care system. Applicants must be under 25, be Mississippi residents, and enroll at least part time. No income requirement applies.

scholarships.name: Freshman Mississippi Resident Academic Scholarship Package
scholarships.amountLabel: $1,000 to $10,500 per year by GPA and ACT
scholarships.description: Automatic award for admitted Mississippi resident freshmen based on ninth through eleventh grade GPA and ACT score. Requires a 3.0 GPA and a 21 ACT to qualify, with larger awards at higher scores. Renewable for four years.

scholarships.name: Academic Merit Scholarship (Mississippi Residents)
scholarships.description: Automatic merit award for admitted Mississippi resident freshmen at Ole Miss. Requires a 3.0 high school GPA and a 23 ACT, with award size rising by ACT score. Superscores are accepted and the award is renewable.

scholarships.name: Mississippi Star Student Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award at Ole Miss recognizing Mississippi students named a STAR Student by their high school for top academic and test performance. Stacks with the automatic merit award for entering resident freshmen.

scholarships.name: Valedictorian and Salutatorian Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award at Ole Miss for Mississippi high school valedictorians and salutatorians. Requires official confirmation of class rank and stacks with other entering freshman merit awards.

scholarships.name: Stamps Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Full cost of attendance plus $12,000 stipend
scholarships.description: The most competitive award at Ole Miss, covering full cost of attendance plus a $12,000 enrichment stipend. Selects Mississippi residents with exceptional academic and leadership records through a competitive application.

scholarships.name: W.R. Newman Scholarship
scholarships.description: Competitive award at Ole Miss for Mississippi residents with strong academics and leadership. Provides $10,000 per year for four years and requires a separate scholarship application by January 10.

scholarships.name: Robert M. Carrier Scholarship
scholarships.description: Competitive Ole Miss award providing $10,000 per year for Mississippi residents with strong academic and leadership credentials. Requires the competitive scholarship application by January 10.

scholarships.name: Ole Miss First Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award at Ole Miss combining academic merit and financial need, providing $4,500 per year with a service and mentoring component. Open to Mississippi resident entering freshmen through the competitive application.

scholarships.name: Chancellor's Leadership Class Scholarship
scholarships.description: First year leadership award at Ole Miss for students nominated by a school official for strong leadership. Includes a leadership development program alongside the scholarship.

scholarships.name: Luckyday Scholars Program (USM)
scholarships.description: Provides $6,000 per year to Mississippi residents entering the University of Southern Mississippi with a history of community involvement. Requires a 3.5 high school GPA and a 20 ACT superscore, and is renewable for four years.

scholarships.name: Luckyday Scholars Program (MSU)
scholarships.description: Selects about 80 Mississippi resident freshmen at Mississippi State each year for up to $6,000 per year with a leadership and service program. Requires a 3.5 GPA, a 20 ACT, and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Ergon, Inc. Scholarship Fund for Engineering
scholarships.organization: Mississippi State University (Bagley College of Engineering)
scholarships.description: Endowed award for students in the Bagley College of Engineering at Mississippi State majoring in mechanical, chemical, or civil and environmental engineering. Requires a minimum 3.0 GPA.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation for Mississippi Scholarships
scholarships.description: A single application matches students to more than a dozen named scholarship funds administered by the Community Foundation for Mississippi in the greater Jackson region. Most funds serve graduating high school seniors.

scholarships.name: CREATE Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: CREATE Foundation administers more than 100 named scholarship funds for students across Northeast Mississippi counties. Individual funds set their own criteria, often tied to specific high schools, fields of study, or counties.

scholarships.name: Robert M. Hearin Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Robert M. Hearin Foundation (University of Southern Mississippi)
scholarships.description: Need based award for full time undergraduate students at the University of Southern Mississippi funded by the Robert M. Hearin Foundation. Selection considers financial need and academic record.

scholarships.name: Mississippi Farm Bureau Federation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for students preparing for careers that benefit agriculture and rural communities in Mississippi. Selection favors students pursuing agriculture related fields of study.

scholarships.name: Mississippi Rural Physicians Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Provides $35,000 per year through medical school to Mississippi students from rural backgrounds who commit to practicing primary care in a rural Mississippi community. Students may apply as undergraduates or as admitted medical students.

scholarships.name: Leland Speed Scholarship
scholarships.description: Covers full tuition for all admitted Mississippi residents at Mississippi College after other aid is applied. Requires meeting the qualifying test score, living on campus, and filing federal and state aid applications.

scholarships.name: Distinguished Young Women of Mississippi
scholarships.description: Scholarship program for high school senior girls in Mississippi judged on scholastics, interview, talent, fitness, and self expression. Local winners receive cash scholarships and the state winner advances to the national program.

scholarships.name: Distinguished Young Women Scholarship (MSU)
scholarships.description: Award at Mississippi State for entering freshmen who participated as a Distinguished Young Women state or local representative. Recognizes the scholastic and leadership record built through the program.

scholarships.name: Agnes Jones Jackson Scholarship
scholarships.description: National NAACP award supporting African American undergraduate and graduate students, open to Mississippi students who are current NAACP members. Considers both academic merit and financial need with a 2.5 GPA minimum for undergraduates.

scholarships.name: Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Major need-based scholarship for Nebraska residents who graduate from a Nebraska high school or earn a Nebraska GED and attend a public Nebraska college or university. Awarded to first-time freshmen who demonstrate financial need. DACA and undocumented students are eligible. Cannot be used at private or out-of-state colleges.

scholarships.name: Nebraska Opportunity Grant (NOG)
scholarships.organization: Nebraska's Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education
scholarships.description: State need-based grant for Nebraska residents with high financial need who have not earned a bachelor's, graduate or professional degree and are attending eligible Nebraska colleges or universities. Awarded through the financial aid office of the student's college based on the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Access College Early (ACE) Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Nebraska's Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education
scholarships.description: State scholarship that funds college dual-enrollment courses for Nebraska high school students with financial need, letting them earn college credit while still in high school at participating Nebraska colleges.

scholarships.name: Community College Gap Assistance Program
scholarships.organization: Nebraska's Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education
scholarships.description: Need-based aid for Nebraska community college students in credit or non-credit workforce programs not eligible for Pell grants that lead to jobs in high-need fields. Family income must be at or below 250 percent of federal poverty guidelines.

scholarships.name: Nebraska Career Scholarship
scholarships.description: State-funded scholarship for students pursuing high-demand majors at UNL including engineering, mathematics, healthcare, information technology, data science, actuarial science, physics, chemistry, psychology, special education and pre-health. Requires a Nebraska-based internship or major-related employment before graduation.

scholarships.name: Nebraska Promise
scholarships.description: Covers full undergraduate tuition at any University of Nebraska campus for Nebraska residents who are Pell-eligible or have family adjusted gross income of $65,000 or less. No separate application; eligibility is determined automatically from the FAFSA. Requires full-time enrollment and a 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: Presidential Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Top merit award for Nebraska resident first-time freshmen enrolling at any University of Nebraska campus. Requires an ACT composite of 36 (or SAT 1570-1600). Covers tuition, fees, books, housing, food, personal and transportation costs plus a $5,000 annual stipend.

scholarships.name: Regents Scholarship
scholarships.amountLabel: Full resident tuition (up to 120 credit hours)
scholarships.description: Prestigious merit award covering full resident tuition at UNL for academically outstanding incoming freshmen who graduated from a Nebraska high school with a GPA of 3.75 or higher. Based on academic record, class rank and test scores; awarded automatically to qualifying admitted students.

scholarships.name: UNK Chancellor's Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship for first-time freshmen who are Nebraska residents entering UNK with a 3.9+ high school GPA and 28+ ACT. Provides $7,000 toward tuition and $2,000 toward campus housing annually, renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Lincoln Community Foundation Student Success Scholarship
scholarships.description: For graduating high school seniors or GED graduates from Lancaster County, Nebraska planning to attend an accredited two-year or four-year nonprofit college. Preference for students attending Nebraska institutions; financial need may be considered. Renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Lincoln Community Foundation Scholarships (all funds)
scholarships.description: Portal to more than 90 scholarship funds administered by the Lincoln Community Foundation benefiting students in Lancaster County and across Nebraska. One general application matches students to many local funds with varying criteria.

scholarships.name: Omaha Public Schools Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for graduating seniors from all Omaha Public Schools high schools, OPS Alternative Programs and the OPS Career Center. A single portal application matches students to many donor-established funds with a range of criteria.

scholarships.name: Union Pacific Latino Employee Network (LEN) Scholarship
scholarships.description: For students of Latino/Hispanic heritage who are residents of Nebraska or Iowa, enrolled in the first four years of an undergraduate or technical degree program, with a 3.0 GPA or higher. Not open to children or dependents of Union Pacific employees.

scholarships.name: Union Pacific Black Employee Network (BEN) Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Black/African American residents of Nebraska (and select other states) who are current high school seniors or college underclassmen. Recipients are selected on scholastic ability, leadership, extracurricular involvement and social awareness.

scholarships.name: Nebraska Press Association Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Nebraska high school graduates enrolling or enrolled at a Nebraska or out-of-state college with a specific interest in community-based print journalism or agricultural communications. Special consideration for involvement in a local community or student newspaper.

scholarships.name: Nebraska Broadcasters Association Foundation EEO Scholarship
scholarships.description: For students enrolled in radio, television broadcasting or broadcast journalism programs at Nebraska colleges. Applicants must have a Nebraska connection (graduated from a Nebraska high school or attend a Nebraska college) and plan a broadcasting career.

scholarships.name: Oxbow Animal Health Nebraska High School Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Nebraska high school seniors planning to attend college in any state to prepare for a career in the companion animal industry, veterinary medicine or animal health. Awarded annually to multiple recipients.

scholarships.name: Nebraska Farm Bureau Foundation County Scholarships
scholarships.description: County-level scholarships for Nebraska high school seniors pursuing college, many focused on agriculture and agribusiness. Award amounts and deadlines vary by county Farm Bureau across the state.

scholarships.name: Husker Harvest Days Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Nebraska graduating high school seniors pursuing a program or career in agriculture, agribusiness or another ag-related field at an accredited university, college or technical school. Nine scholarships awarded each year.

scholarships.name: Foundation of the Nebraska Society of CPAs Scholarship
scholarships.description: For accounting majors at Nebraska colleges and universities who plan to sit for the CPA exam and are considering an accounting career in Nebraska. Awarded to students who have completed their junior year via department nomination.

scholarships.name: Ponca Tribe Adam Way Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For enrolled members of the Ponca Tribe of Nebraska, ages 18 to 45, currently residing in Nebraska and seeking to further their education. Administered by the Tribe's Education Department.

scholarships.name: Ponca Tribe Building for the Future Scholarship
scholarships.description: Education scholarship for enrolled members of the Ponca Tribe of Nebraska pursuing higher education, administered by the Tribe's Education Department.

scholarships.name: Ponca Tribe Higher Education Grant
scholarships.description: Higher education financial aid for enrolled Ponca tribal members attending college or receiving training in the United States. Quarterly application deadlines administered by the Tribe's Education Department.

scholarships.name: Standing Bear Scholarship
scholarships.description: For members of a federally recognized Native American tribe eligible for resident tuition at the University of Nebraska who hold an undergraduate degree and are admitted as full-time students at the University of Nebraska College of Law. Covers tuition, books and fees.

scholarships.name: Mid-Nebraska Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: One application matches Nebraska students to more than 100 scholarship funds administered by the Mid-Nebraska Community Foundation, serving students of all ages and educational interests across the region.

scholarships.name: McCook Community Foundation Fund Scholarships
scholarships.description: Local scholarships for students in the McCook, Nebraska area administered by the McCook Community Foundation Fund, an affiliated fund of the Nebraska Community Foundation, with criteria set by individual donors.

scholarships.name: Nebraska Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Statewide network connecting Nebraska students to scholarship funds held by 252 affiliated community funds. Each fund sets its own purpose, eligibility, award level and location where scholarships can be used; students register on the scholarship portal to apply.

scholarships.name: New Mexico Legislative Lottery Scholarship
scholarships.description: Tuition assistance for New Mexico residents who graduate from a New Mexico high school and enroll full time at a New Mexico public college or university within 16 months. Students must earn and maintain a 2.5 GPA and full-time enrollment.

scholarships.name: New Mexico Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: Covers tuition and fees not met by other aid at New Mexico public colleges and universities and tribal colleges. Open to New Mexico residents including returning adult learners and those ineligible for the Lottery Scholarship.

scholarships.name: Teacher Preparation Affordability Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Assists New Mexico residents pursuing teacher licensure through an accredited teacher preparation program, including alternative certification and graduate education programs. Awards are based on financial need, up to five years.

scholarships.name: New Mexico Native American Tuition Scholarship
scholarships.description: Covers up to full in-state tuition for enrolled members of a New Mexico tribe who are New Mexico residents attending eligible public institutions in bordering states. Priority to New Mexico high school graduates.

scholarships.name: New Mexico Gas Company Native American Scholarship
scholarships.description: Twenty scholarships of $3,000 each for enrolled members of a New Mexico Pueblo, Tribe, or Nation living in New Mexico. Open to graduating high school seniors, GED holders, and current college or trade school students.

scholarships.name: LANL Foundation Four-Year Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: For high school seniors and undergraduates from seven Northern New Mexico counties (Los Alamos, Mora, Rio Arriba, San Miguel, Sandoval, Santa Fe, Taos) and Northern NM tribes. Requires a 3.25 unweighted GPA; preference to first-generation students.

scholarships.name: LANL Foundation National Security Workforce Graduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: For graduate students pursuing advanced degrees aligned with national security careers at Los Alamos National Laboratory, enrolled or planning to enroll at New Mexico colleges and universities. Up to eight awards annually.

scholarships.name: Daniels Scholarship Program
scholarships.amountLabel: Up to a full four-year scholarship
scholarships.description: Up to a full-ride four-year scholarship for graduating high school seniors in New Mexico, Colorado, Utah, or Wyoming with strong character, leadership, and community commitment. Requires a 3.0 GPA and family AGI of $100,000 or less.

scholarships.name: Andrew Piech Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For current or past New Mexico residents pursuing an automotive or technical vocational degree or certificate at a nonprofit or public institution. One to two awards annually.

scholarships.name: Bob Chavez Scholarship for the Arts
scholarships.description: For New Mexico high school seniors or college students affiliated with a federally recognized New Mexico Pueblo who are pursuing visual arts or a related field. Requires a 2.0 GPA.

scholarships.name: Carl F. Scott Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For New Mexico residents from Quay County who are high school seniors or continuing college students pursuing two-year, four-year, or advanced degrees.

scholarships.name: Davis-Kozoll Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Northwest New Mexico high school seniors pursuing a science or human service degree or a trade or vocational certificate. Requires a minimum 2.0 GPA, with preference for specific rural communities.

scholarships.name: Joe "Isi" Trujillo Scholarship
scholarships.description: For graduates of Hot Springs High School in Truth or Consequences attending a New Mexico public university, college, or community college full time. Requires a minimum 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: James Knott Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For New Mexico high school seniors living in a manufactured or mobile home. Requires a minimum 3.0 GPA and proof of residency. One to two awards annually.

scholarships.name: New Mexico Veterans Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For New Mexico high school seniors (public, private, charter, or homeschool) planning to attend a nonprofit or public college, university, community college, or trade school. Requires a minimum 2.0 GPA and an essay on Medal of Honor core values.

scholarships.name: Nina J. Wing Scholarship
scholarships.description: For students previously in foster care for at least one year who graduated from a New Mexico high school and attend Central New Mexico Community College. Requires a minimum 2.0 GPA; up to $24,000 cumulative.

scholarships.name: Sussman-Miller Educational Assistance Fund
scholarships.description: Fills the financial aid gap of $500 to $8,000 for New Mexico high school seniors (3.5 GPA) or current undergraduates (3.0 GPA) who receive federal financial aid and attend a nonprofit institution full time.

scholarships.name: David R. Woodling Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For New Mexico legal residents of at least one year pursuing metals technology with a machine tool or welding concentration at a nonprofit or public institution. High school seniors require a 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: Manuel Lujan Excellence in Education Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For seniors from 24 designated central New Mexico high schools attending a New Mexico four-year college or university full time. Requires a minimum 2.5 GPA; renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Kiwanis Club of Albuquerque Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For seniors in the Albuquerque metro area (Bernalillo, Sandoval, Valencia, Torrance Counties) with a minimum 3.0 GPA and strong community service, with preference for early childhood development or teaching careers.

scholarships.name: Susie Kubie Symphonic Music Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Albuquerque Youth Symphony Program participants who graduated from an Albuquerque metro high school and are pursuing a music degree with full-time enrollment. Renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Woodcock Family Education Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: For Albuquerque metro area seniors (Bernalillo, Sandoval, Valencia, Torrance Counties) with a minimum 3.8 GPA and strong math and science credentials enrolling full time. Renewable for four years.

scholarships.name: Barnes W. Rose, Jr. and Eva Rose Nickol Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For Albuquerque High School seniors pursuing a STEM degree in science, technology, engineering, or mathematics. Requires a minimum 3.6 GPA.

scholarships.name: William F. Mann Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Albuquerque High School students with a minimum 2.5 GPA, a strong community service background, and stand-up citizen characteristics. One to two awards, renewable up to four years.

scholarships.name: Rae Lee Siporin Scholarship for Women
scholarships.description: For female New Mexico residents completing their senior year after an educational break, with a minimum 2.0 GPA, demonstrated financial need, and the ability to graduate within three semesters.

scholarships.name: AAF-NM Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For New Mexico resident junior or senior undergraduates or graduate students with a 3.0 GPA who maintain a marketing internship and attend a New Mexico four-year nonprofit or public institution.

scholarships.name: Anne and Tony Hillerman Scholarship
scholarships.organization: New Mexico Press Women (via Albuquerque Community Foundation)
scholarships.description: For New Mexico or out-of-state undergraduates and graduates studying journalism or communications at New Mexico institutions, enrolled for the fall semester. Requires portfolio samples, resume, transcript, and references.

scholarships.name: Rosenstiel Scholarship
scholarships.organization: New Mexico Press Women (via Albuquerque Community Foundation)
scholarships.description: For New Mexico graduate students in journalism, communications, or law interested in First Amendment issues or investigative journalism. Requires a minimum 3.0 GPA, portfolio, resume, transcript, and references.

scholarships.name: Learning Basket Scholarship
scholarships.description: For American Indian or Alaska Native students in the final year of a master's counseling program with an internship, or newly licensed counselors within two years. Requires a 3.2 GPA and Tribal or Pueblo affiliation.

scholarships.name: James Ledwith Memorial Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For Albuquerque metro area high school seniors (Bernalillo, Valencia, Torrance, Sandoval Counties) who have overcome an extraordinary life challenge while demonstrating hope, faith, and courage. One to two awards.

scholarships.name: Youth in Foster Care Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For New Mexico residents of at least one year who have been in the New Mexico foster care system for at least one year, ages 17 to 21, with a minimum 2.5 GPA in high school or college.

scholarships.name: Michael S. Currier Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarships for low-income students from northern New Mexico pursuing an undergraduate degree at an accredited institution. Requires a minimum 3.5 GPA and full-time enrollment.

scholarships.name: Albuquerque Hispano Chamber Excellence in Education Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Albuquerque Hispano Chamber of Commerce Foundation
scholarships.description: Recognizes graduating Hispanic high school seniors and current college students from across New Mexico entering higher education or trade school, awarding for educational achievement and leadership. More than $3 million awarded over 39 years.

scholarships.name: New Mexico Scholars Program
scholarships.description: Covers tuition, required fees, and books for high-achieving New Mexico high school graduates from families under an income cap who enroll full time at an eligible New Mexico public college or university. Merit and need based.

scholarships.name: New Mexico Firefighters and Peace Officers Survivors Scholarship
scholarships.description: Waives tuition and fees at New Mexico public postsecondary institutions for the spouse and children of New Mexico firefighters and peace officers killed in the line of duty.

scholarships.name: Governor Guinn Millennium Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awards Nevada high school graduates who attend an eligible Nevada college or university. Pays a set amount per credit hour depending on institution type. No application required; eligible students are submitted by their Nevada high school.

scholarships.name: Silver State Opportunity Grant (SSOG)
scholarships.description: Nevada's state-funded need-based grant for low-income, college-ready students at a Nevada community or state college. Requires FAFSA and Nevada residency for tuition purposes.

scholarships.name: Nevada Promise Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Nevada System of Higher Education / College of Southern Nevada
scholarships.description: Last-dollar scholarship covering up to three years of community college tuition and mandatory fees not paid by other gift aid. Open to Nevada residents regardless of income or GPA; requires training, FAFSA, and community service.

scholarships.name: UNLV Nevada Resident Institutional Aid
scholarships.description: UNLV covers tuition, fees, and $1,000 toward books for eligible full-time Nevada resident first-year students with adjusted gross income under $68,000 who file the FAFSA or Institutional Aid Application by the priority deadline.

scholarships.name: Nevada Women's Fund Degree Pathway Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for women residing in northern or rural Nevada (all counties except Clark) pursuing an associate, bachelor, master, or doctorate degree. Requires FAFSA and transcript.

scholarships.name: Nevada Women's Fund Workforce Ready Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarships for women in northern or rural Nevada pursuing certificate programs, trade or vocational training, continuing education, or licensure. No GPA requirement; quarterly applications.

scholarships.name: Latin Chamber of Commerce Community Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Latin Chamber of Commerce Community Foundation
scholarships.description: Competitive scholarship for first-generation students pursuing STEM or business and finance degrees, with demonstrated financial need. Requires enrollment in a foundation cohort and a service commitment each semester.

scholarships.name: Hannah Brown CDC Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Urban Chamber of Commerce / Hannah Brown Community Development Corporation
scholarships.description: Scholarship for graduating Nevada high school seniors entering college, university, or trade school. Requires a leadership essay and two recommendation letters; partnership serving the local community since 1999.

scholarships.name: AAUW Las Vegas Branch Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for full-time women juniors or seniors (60+ credits) in a bachelor's program at Nevada State University, UNLV, or College of Southern Nevada. Recipients also receive AAUW student membership and mentoring.

scholarships.name: Las Vegas Southwest Rotary Club Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Rotary Club of Las Vegas Southwest
scholarships.description: Renewable four-year scholarships (John & Lou Yoxen and Adrienne Cox awards) for graduating Clark County seniors attending a Nevada public college or university. A one-year Barry Smith award is also offered.

scholarships.name: Frias Legacy Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Public Education Foundation / Charles and Phyllis M. Frias Charitable Trust
scholarships.description: Awards Clark County high school seniors, with the top award covering a full four-year degree. Administered through the Public Education Foundation's Scholarships Plus program.

scholarships.name: NV Energy Powerful Partnerships Scholarship
scholarships.organization: NV Energy Foundation / Community Foundation of Northern Nevada
scholarships.description: One-time scholarships for graduating high school seniors in NV Energy's northern Nevada service territory, usable at any accredited Nevada college, community college, or trade school. Dependents of NV Energy employees are considered for separate $2,000 awards.

scholarships.name: Caesars Nevada Team Member Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for children of Caesars Entertainment employees in Nevada, particularly wage and tip earners. Administered through the Community Foundation of Northern Nevada scholarship portal.

scholarships.name: Don Carano Legacy Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for dependents of Caesars Entertainment employees at grade 14 or below with at least two years of service. Applied for through the Community Foundation of Northern Nevada portal.

scholarships.name: Claudine Williams Harrah's Las Vegas Employee Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for high school seniors or college students whose parent or guardian has worked at Harrah's Las Vegas (grade L14 or below) for three consecutive years. Administered via the Community Foundation of Northern Nevada.

scholarships.name: Meruelo Family Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for dependents of full-time Grand Sierra Resort & Casino and Sahara Las Vegas employees with at least one year of tenure. Administered through the Community Foundation of Northern Nevada portal.

scholarships.name: Foster Children Education Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Nevada foster care graduates with a 3.0 or higher GPA pursuing higher education. Administered through the Community Foundation of Northern Nevada scholarship portal.

scholarships.name: Otto A. Huth Scholarship Fund
